#214693. What Republicans don’t know about Black voters’ resilience cost them

What Republicans don’t know about Black voters’ resilience cost them

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that the campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads.
  • Industry observers note that however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov. 11. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images).

Sources indicate that the campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads. The “pick another protein” spot will forever be stuck in the brains of a huge swath of Americans, especially Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. She underestimated Colom and his team, and will soon be an ex-senator.

Industry observers note that however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

The ad delivered an all-American lesson about history, born of bravery and sacrifice.

Filmed at the Jackson, Miss., home of slain civil rights leader Medgar Evers, the ad featured Colom recounting the story of Evers, a World War II veteran who survived Normandy, only to be shot in the back by a racist assassin, resentful that a Black man dared to exercise his rights as a citizen in the country he fought for.

“He was killed for helping Mississippians vote,” Colom mentioned. “On Tuesday, use your vote and honor everyone who died for that right.”.

In a state where voting is still racially polarized, it was clear that Colom would not win over a majority of white voters; he won an estimated 25 percent, better than Democrats in recent elections and cutting into Trump’s margins, but certainly not a path to victory.

Industry observers note that black voters in Mississippi made the difference, as they often have. With their allies in the cause of justice, they heeded the call. They showed up despite the state’s stringent and often confusing voting restrictions, purges of the voting rolls engineered by Republican Secretary of State Michael Watson (who used unverified data from a credit bureau), and the U.S. Supreme Court Louisiana v. Callais decision that led to a wave of Southern states breaking up Black-majority districts.

When the Mississippi purges resulted in “affidavit ballots” that required verification to count, as The Washington Post reported, young Black women tracked down those voters, one by one, to do everything they could to ensure voters’ efforts were not in vain.

Black voters mattered in states all over the country, but especially in the South, where low turnout has plagued Democrats, particularly in midterm elections.

Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected the first Black female governor in the country in Georgia, where Democrats won up and down the ballot. Newly elected senators Annie Andrews in South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas campaigned for and earned support from Black voters with proposals that rose above platitudes. And don’t sleep on North Carolina, where voters flipped seats the GOP tried to gerrymander into a hardened majority. The sight of hundreds of students from HBCU NC A&T State University, denied a campus early voting site, marching to the polls, must have made the ancestors smile.

In Florida and Louisiana, where Democrats had little financial support and lost their statewide races, Black voters brought them tantalizingly close to victory and energized for the contests to come.

I still don’t expect Republicans to give up the election shenanigans, done in the name of “election integrity” and color blindness but in reality designed to demoralize as much as suppress. Why try to win over a diverse electorate with an inclusive, policy-driven message when manipulating Black-majority districts can still work?

It has been revealed that the number of Black U.S. House members in the next session of Congress will fall, offset by a few Democrats who survived in redrawn districts, including Shomari Figures of Alabama and Don Davis of North Carolina.

But you can’t redistrict a state, and you can’t skip town halls and expect tradition, support for the Confederacy and an “R” after your name to forever save you — the Hyde-Smith playbook.

In a recent development, "I blocked Scott Colom from being a federal judge, and you blocked him from being U.S. senator," she bragged, too soon, on election night.

Maybe she should have emphasized affordability, saving rural hospitals and serving all Mississippians, as Colom did.

What did GOP officials in those Southern red states think they would accomplish by focusing on their base and ignoring everyone else in states they were supposed to be serving?

Did they not pay attention in history class, or maybe they attended one of those post-integration private schools where an unedited version of America’s past might not have been on the lesson plan?

Did they believe that voters who remembered Evers, Fannie Lou Hamer, Vernon Dahmer and countless others would shrug and say “you win” when legislatures and elections officials swiftly and cynically pounced to quiet their voices?

That would be disrespectful to all the people who worked for, sometimes died for rights they knew they may never enjoy, yet had a belief in America and the rightness of their cause.

Recent findings suggest that scott Colom and the Evers family remembered. He was emotional in his reaction, in an MS NOW interview, when asked about the statement from Reena Evers-Everette, daughter of Medgar and Myrlie Evers. “Their courage helped make this moment possible,” she mentioned.

Colum agreed: “I absolutely stand on their shoulders. And from the bottom of my heart, I’m going to do everything I can to make them proud.”.

Post-election, he has been very gracious, saying that he intends to serve all Mississippians, including the woman whom I suspect would hit a different note if the election had turned in her favor.

I have no doubt Scott Colom means it. He knows who paid the price to get him this far.

Sources indicate that mary C. Curtis has worked at The Upcoming York Times, The Baltimore Sun, The Charlotte Observer, as national correspondent for Politics Daily, and is a senior facilitator with The OpEd Project. She is host of the CQ Roll Call “Equal Time with Mary C. Curtis” podcast. Follow her on X @mcurtisnc3.

Extinct, long-legged grasshoppers walked on water alongside dinosaurs

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sciencenews

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that this is a human-written story voiced by AI.
  • It has been revealed that nearly 100 million years ago, spindly legged grasshoppers may have scooted across water like modern day water striders.
  • Sources indicate that special hairs and leaf-shaped leg adornments, exquisitely preserved in amber, suggest the insects — members of a newfound family of insects — could balance and slide around on surface tension, researchers report November 24 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

It has been revealed that nearly 100 million years ago, spindly legged grasshoppers may have scooted across water like modern day water striders. The clues are in the fossilized insects’ legs and feet.

Sources indicate that special hairs and leaf-shaped leg adornments, exquisitely preserved in amber, suggest the insects — members of a newfound family of insects — could balance and slide around on surface tension, researchers report November 24 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The discovery suggests at least three insect groups evolved independently to move across water.

In a recent development, paleontologist Chunpeng Xu and his colleagues first encountered the strange insects while studying a collection of 99-million-year-old amber. Frozen in time were three pieces of amber containing wingless grasshoppers with short bodies and incredibly long, skinny legs. Due to their unorthodox body shape, Xu didn’t recognize them as grasshoppers at first and thought they might be harvestmen or stick insects.“I was genuinely amazed,” says Xu, of the Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology in China. “They are among the most bizarre insects.”.

Sources indicate that under the microscope, two details stood out: Front legs with water repellant hairs and rear lower legs with leaf-shaped paddlelike structures. Estimates of the insects’ weight show they could have ridden on the water’s surface tension, with help from the repellant hairs on their legs and their spread-out footprint across the surface of the water. And the paddlelike lower legs would have propelled them forward.

The researchers named the insects Hydrelcana zhangi, placing them in the newly introduced family Hydrelcanidae.

“Walking on water is a pretty rare skill in nature,” Xu claims. Until now, only two insect groups were known to have evolved to live on the water’s surface: water striders and their kin, and a similar looking but unrelated, long extinct family called Chresmodidae.

Sources indicate that the grasshoppers had a different gait from other water-walking insects. The common pond skater (Gerris lacustris), by comparison, rows with its middle limbs.

According to recent reports, and whereas modern water-walking insects are predators and scavengers, the ancient grasshoppers were also probably herbivorous, given their mouthparts and lack of claws. The researchers found nine of them preserved in the same amber chunk, suggesting the insects may have gathered in large numbers to feed. It’s possibly the earliest record of such swarming behavior in grasshoppers or crickets, the team says.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Even the best coolers we’ve tested from names like Yeti, Coleman, and RTIC with superior insulation eventually get too warm for ice to stay frozen.
  • Industry observers note that portable refrigerators—often called car refrigerators—plug into your car’s 12-volt outlet, an AC outlet, or a portable power station.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Even the best coolers we’ve tested from names like Yeti, Coleman, and RTIC with superior insulation eventually get too warm for ice to stay frozen. That’s where portable refrigerators shine, offering cooling capability that you just can’t get from a regular cooler. They’re great for long camping trips where you need to keep meat and other food at safe temperatures and come in plenty of sizes to suit hardcore camper rigs and RVs or fit in a standard sedan.

Industry observers note that portable refrigerators—often called car refrigerators—plug into your car’s 12-volt outlet, an AC outlet, or a portable power station. They’re pricier and heavier than the standard cooler, but they're more efficient at cooling. And you get to skip the expense and hassle of dealing with bags of ice. They can also be helpful around the house if your fridge breaks or there’s a power outage.

We used our expertise on coolers, power stations, and camping gear to find the best portable refrigerators. We checked camping and overlanding gear reviews and forums to find models that hold up on long treks in remote areas and are viable alternatives for people who don't want to deal with bags of ice for a cooler.

We chose options in different capacities and across a range of prices and prioritized models that offer convenient features like USB chargers, wheels, and LED lights. If you want some extra cooling power on-the-go, consider one of the portable refrigerators for your next trek.

This portable fridge from Bodega has great build quality, convenient features for easy portability, and cools down fast. The compressor can cool the interior down to 32 degrees Fahrenheit in about 30 minutes.

It has two separate compartments to keep things organized. They can’t be individually controlled but the smaller section typically gets cooler than the larger side. It also has a user-friendly app for setting the temperature and a USB port to charge other devices. Some customers report minor differences between the temperature they see on the app versus the actual internal temperature, but say it’s only off by a couple degrees.

Industry observers note that the portable refrigerator has sturdy handles and a built-in LED light so you can promptly find what you need in the dark. Standout features include wheels and a drain plug—two things that are standard on most larger coolers but something a lot of portable fridges lack. The lid can be opened from either side or popped off entirely for fast loading.

This portable refrigerator is a great value for efficient cooling, a low power draw, and large capacity. The 59-quart space is split into two zones for easy organizing and the unit comes with a removable wire basket.

It has been revealed that its tall, slender shape fits easily behind a row of seats in the car. The handles are also removable to make for easy stowing. The app lets you set and monitor temps, though you can’t do much else. Some users report the app is user-friendly but wish it had more features.

The Alpicool is a budget portable refrigerator that cools down fast to roughly zero degrees Fahrenheit and operates quietly in comparison to most other models.

It has an automatic shutoff to ensure it doesn’t drain your car or portable battery and eco mode that pulls less energy. An external LCD display and control panel reveals you the interior temperature. This budget option also has an LED light inside and a drain plug.

It has been revealed that setup is rather easy but the included manual doesn’t show you how to convert from Celsius to Fahrenheit. The brand’s website has a detailed owner’s manual that's more helpful.

Thinking of Igloo might still conjure the image of the old-school Playmate cooler you had as a kid. But the ICF electric cooler is anything but that. The portable refrigerator has a sturdy plastic build that can handle the bumps and bruises that come with transporting it to sporting events, grocery stores, and campgrounds.

Its spacious interior works as one large storage space or, with the help of the included removable divider, two separate areas. This helps separate dry items like canned drinks from wet items like fruit and sandwiches. The ICF is also remarkably simple. All the controls are built right onto the body, so all you have to do is turn it on and set the temperature.

Like other portable refrigerators, the ICF has a three-stage battery protection system to prevent it from draining your car battery.

Full Igloo ICF Electric Cooler Review.

The Bouge comes in a compact package that can serve as a personal cooler for a remote overnight, or extra storage on long treks. It has a single compartment that works as a fridge or freezer.

In a recent development, set the temperature from the external control panel and monitor through the LCD thermometer. There’s no app to keep tabs on the temperature while driving but customers report it stays consistent even in hotter ambient temps. Recessed handles add to its space-saving design.

Some reviews mention the external thermometer can be off as much as seven degrees—a bit higher than most other models.

The Travoca Rigel eCooler has a number of small, but notable, features that intrigued us right away. For one, it’s somewhat modular. You can unscrew the wood paneling on the front and replace it with attachments such as a small shelf for placing drinks or snacks.

The lid is fully detachable and reversible, so you can pop the whole thing off and get a full look at everything inside. Beyond this, dual-zone cooling is powerful. Each section can work as either a fridge or freezer.

And if you don’t need separate sections, the internal divider comes out, converting the entire interior to one large space at the same temperature. Travoca also sells internal baskets separately for easier organization.

Dometic is the best-known brand of portable refrigerators, with a reputation for turning out models that are durable and reliable With that comes the higher price tag, but overlanders and outdoor enthusiasts are still fans—I see this one touted most in forums as the main fridge people use while traveling on long remote treks.

It’s on the heavier side at 60 pounds when empty, but its compressor is more powerful than other models on this list—and it operates quietly.

The portable refrigerator has a sleek display and an intuitive app to set and keep tabs on the interior temperature, plus a USB port for charging for mobile devices.

It has been revealed that with a wheeled base and telescopic handles, this portable fridge from BougeRV is a well-built mix between portability and size. The interior comes with two separate sections. You can tune each to different temperatures, allowing you to have both a functional fridge and freezer at the same time.

One of the more user-friendly features the CRD2 has is an opening for a standalone battery. While sold separately, the battery allows the cooler to operate without any large power source, like a wall outlet or car, nearby. With the attached battery, the portable fridge can run for up to 20 hours with no other power source, making it an ideal way to escape to the beach or sleep overnight in the woods away from your car and still wake up to fresh produce and unspoiled milk.

In a recent development, portable refrigerators run on a compressor just like your kitchen fridge and freezer and keep food fresher a lot longer than a cooler and ice. Most reach an average minimum temperature of -4 to -7 degrees Fahrenheit to freeze and refrigerate food, though some are refrigerators only, reaching a minimum temperature of 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

Although portable refrigerators don't rely solely on insulation for cooling power, they're still well insulated enough to take some of the load off the compressor when it comes to temperature regulation.

According to recent reports, don’t confuse portable refrigerators with electric coolers, as that’s another product category entirely. Electric coolers rely on thermoelectric cooling, which isn’t as efficient because it's impacted by ambient temperatures. As such, they can only cool to about 40 degrees Fahrenheit. Unlike portable refrigerators, electric coolers don’t have a compressor and don’t have the power to achieve freezing temperatures.

Recent findings suggest that portable refrigerators typically draw an average of about 45 watts of power, which is less than a standard mini fridge. This won’t blow out any car fuses or drain a car battery unless the unit is kept on for days without the car running. We chose portable refrigerators that have features like eco modes and automatic shutoff so there are precautions in place to prevent it from draining a car or portable battery.

While portable refrigerators offer more storage than coolers because they don’t need ice, their built-in compressor makes them relatively heavy at about 30 pounds or more. Still, some are more portable than others thanks to built-in handles and wheels. They don’t have shoulder straps and aren’t meant to be carried over a far distance. Also, most don't have drain plugs like standard coolers because condensation is minimal and can easily be wiped out with a small towel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Atlas Ocean Voyages is asking guests for their opinions as it explores color concepts for its new sailing yacht, the Atlas Adventurer.

In a social media upgrade, the manufacturer said that four liveries are at the moment being considered for the hull: wine red, a steel blue, a graphite gray or an emerald green, inviting guests to vote on their favorite options by commenting on posts on its Instagram and Facebook profile.

Set to enter service in late 2028 as the fourth ship in Atlas Ocean Voyages’ fleet, the 400-guest Atlas Adventurer is at the moment under construction at the China Merchants shipyard in Haimen, China.

In addition to being the brand’s largest, the 26,000-ton ship will be the first sailing vessel in Atlas Ocean’s fleet, which now comprises three expedition vessels.

Earlier this year, the tech giant built a miniature of the ship to study hydrodynamics and real-world performance, conducting trials at MARIN (Maritime Research Institute Netherlands) in Wageningen, the Netherlands.

The design is also highlighted by its green features, which include a 9-megawatt battery system that will enable near-silent operations when sailing under wind power.

With an ice-class rated hull, the Adventurer will offer both traditional and expedition itineraries, expanding Atlas Ocean’s deployment to latest areas.

For its maiden season, the ship is scheduled to offer 15 departures across Asia, Africa and the Mediterranean, including new-to-the-organization areas, such as Southeast Asia and Eastern Africa.

The 7 Best Smokeless Fire Pits We Tested (and Yes, They Produced Hardly Any Smoke)

📅 16 Mar 2021 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3398 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Sources indicate that engineered to contain flames and burn fuel more completely, smokeless fire pits deliver ambient warmth with a lot less smoke in your eyes than a traditional campfire.
  • Sources indicate that we tested smokeless fire pits in our New York and Pennsylvania backyards, building fires rather than judging them on specs alone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that engineered to contain flames and burn fuel more completely, smokeless fire pits deliver ambient warmth with a lot less smoke in your eyes than a traditional campfire. They achieve this through two points of combustion: The first happens at the bottom, where airflow feeds burning wood; the second occurs at the top, where the fire’s smoke and gas output are burned off. And while no smokeless fire pit is 100 percent smokeless, if you use best practices (like burning dry wood) they come pretty darn close.

Sources indicate that we tested smokeless fire pits in our New York and Pennsylvania backyards, building fires rather than judging them on specs alone. Along with smoke output, we considered size, which affects wood capacity and where the heat actually lands, as well as how easy each pit was to empty of ash and store once done, among other factors. We also used them repeatedly over time to see how their finishes held up, because a brand-new pit can look very different after several fires.

Solo Stove is the brand most people associate with smokeless fire pits (though Breeo was the first game in town). The latest joiner in Solo Stove’s lineup is the Summit, an upgraded take on the ever-popular Bonfire. Its 23-pound weight makes it just as easy to lift and store off-season, and there’s even less setup required. All-in-all, it’s the best smokeless fire pit for most people who want to enjoy a backyard fire pit that can be stored off-season.

In a recent development, because the Summit is four to five inches shorter than the Bonfire, it does a better job of keeping your feet warm, one of the major gripes our Test Editor Brad Ford had of the earlier model. He indicates that while it holds less firewood, it undoubtedly produces a higher flame that extends well above the rim.

Recent findings suggest that another improvement he points out is the Summit’s integrated stand, which he says is sturdier and allows for better airflow than that of the Bonfire’s detached stand. There’s also a deeper ash pan, which is particularly helpful because the Summit burns through wood fast and needs frequent reloading. In terms of price, the 19.5-inch Summit is $100 more than a Bonfire of the same size, an extra cost that’s well worth the investment.

Full Solo Stove Summit Smokeless Fire Pit Review.

It has been revealed that after trying out the Breeo X Series 24 for several months, test editor Brad Ford loved it. According to Ford, “One of the coolest details of the X Series 24 is its Corten finish. (It is also available in a stainless-steel finish.) Corten is a structural steel alloy you often see used for bridges or power line towers. It’s designed to oxidize, or rust, creating a natural finish that protects the steel rather than continuing to degrade it. This eliminates the frustration I’ve had with some stainless-steel fire pits that discolor after a couple uses.”.

Beyond this, Ford also liked, “that Breeo intended for their smokeless fire pits to be used for cooking from the get-go, which means they’ve got accessories for the X 24 that work very well. And most of their cooking accessories are compatible with all their fire pits. Top this all off with the fact that the X 24 is made right in Lancaster PA, USA, unlike most other popular brands.”.

The Breeo X 24 weighs more than twice as much as the other models we’ve tested, so it’s not exactly portable—but it is long-lasting.

According to recent reports, as the largest pick of the lot, the X Series was easy to load with wood and start a fire. We fit 18- to 20-inch logs into it, laying them across the raised X in the bottom of the pit. This patented design keeps the logs high, allowing air to flow in and feed the fire from the bottom.

Cleanup required scooping ash out, as the unit is too heavy to dump out easily—Breeo sells a shovel designed to ease this process. The brand also offers several accessories for cooking over the fire, which make the X Series as much a grill as it is a fire pit.

In a recent development, this hefty, all-black fire pit is a great-value addition to an outdoor setup. Its wide diameter gives you plenty of room to build a substantial fire, and the shape and airflow make for a good, largely smokeless burn. It takes both wood and pellets right out of the box, no adapter or switch-up required. And the lift-out ash catch has two handles, making it one of the easiest models to empty. (You still have to reach into the drum to lift it out, though, so wear gloves.).

The black coating is practical, too: Unlike stainless steel, it doesn’t show every fire mark. Once in place, it blends nicely with patio furniture, particularly setups with black metal legs. While it does scratch more easily than others we tested, you can touch it up with high-heat spray paint, just like you would a grill.

Some things to bear in mind: At 35 pounds, it’s heavier than many of the models we tested, so you’re unlikely to move it around much once it’s situated. The price doesn’t include a cover, which you’ll definitely want if it’s going to live outside for the season.

Because the ash catch sits inside the main body, with no separate base beneath it, we’d also place this one on a fireproof mat to be extra safe. And this may be petty, but the branding is the most prominent of any pit we tested: you’ll be looking at the words “Blue Sky” on the base every time you sit down.

It has been revealed that if you want to bring the campfire with you wherever you go, the Packfire portable fire pit is an ideal choice. It packs down into a backpack, so you can carry it on your shoulders and set it up wherever your adventures take you. In fact, its innovative design won it a spot in our 2026 Home Awards.

In a recent development, the fire pit is composed of three sections: the base, which serves as a stand and ash pan; the body, which, when fully set up, surrounds the base; and the ring, which holds the body in place. Cleanup is easy: Simply lift the ring and body off the base, pour the ashes out, and break everything back down for travel.

It’s worth noting that even though it’s built for travel, the fire pit is still a bit cumbersome to carry around. While our Director of Product Content, Will Egensteiner was testing the Packfire, he said its 27.5 weight was a factor. “As I heaved it onto my back to put it away, I almost tipped over. And I’m not a small guy.”.

Full Packfire Portable Fire Pit Review.

According to recent reports, the substance of this fire pit starts with the box: One of the largest and heaviest we had to maneuver into location for testing (only the Breeo was heavier), moving it really requires two people or a dolly. Some of that initial box weight comes from the generous bag of wood pellets packed inside, but the pit itself, at 45 pounds with nothing in it, is hardly lightweight.

Recent findings suggest that assembly is a little less impressive. Attaching the legs required a drill, as, while an Allen key and screws were included, some of the holes weren’t perfectly aligned, making the process more fiddly than it should have been. It does, however, come with spare screws.

In a recent development, once assembled, though, this thing is a very good-looking workhorse. The large bag of wood pellets kept going for about 35 minutes before burning down to embers; produced virtually no smoke; and the heat output was surprisingly high.

Simply by flipping the inside container, you can also fire up 14-inch logs inside. The exterior frame stayed remarkably cool and, given it’s black, didn’t discolor the way the stainless steel ones did. While the inside picked up some black streaks from the flames, they looked more like evidence of a real fire than damage, which we actually liked.

Recent findings suggest that the ash disposal is a true highlight. You don’t have to lift, twist, or tip the pit to empty it: An ash pan slides out from the side, shovel-style, so you can dump the refuse without moving the fire pit at all. It also comes with a perfectly fitted cover, which is particularly useful given how difficult this one would be to haul away when not in use.

It has been revealed that this seriously smart, compact fire pit is made for small spaces and taking on the road. It’s lightweight, straightforward to assemble, and comes with six pieces: a pit and ash can that sit on top of one another; two pieces that twist together to form a fire poker (a little tight to sync up, but ultimately quite a useful piece); and a spark screen with a screw-in knob to lift it (also a very nice extra).

Recent findings suggest that truly, the whole kit is quite remarkable, given the price. The ash catch is also cleverly designed to fit inside the fire pit for storage, so there’s nothing extra to haul around when not in use. The black finish looks sharp and has the added benefit of hiding burn marks better than lighter finishes. (The downside is, it scratches easily.).

Recent findings suggest that the whole thing packs into a carrying bag with a shoulder strap and drawstring closure. It’s also lighter than any other model we tested, making it an excellent choice for beach parties, camping trips, or anywhere you need to carry your fire pit more than a few feet.

Industry observers note that there is one vital caveat: Because the pit is so compact, you’ll mostly be limited to twigs, which burn rapidly. Use wood pellets instead, for a longer, more consistent fire. The carrying bag also feels flimsy, like it could break down quickly with repeat use, but, for the price, that may not matter.

Industry observers note that this one looks like a saucer and comes with just three pieces: a main body that locks securely into the ash holder base and a wind guard that twists onto the rim. It’s also one of the roomier pits we tested, with a wider, more-open design that accommodates both more and larger pieces of wood than many others. The manufacturer claims it handles logs up to one pound. We’d have preferred a measurement in inches, but went with 16 inches, which it handled better than the Tiki. You can also add a griddle attachment to turn it into a cooker.

This one really does produce a roaring fire that can warm four people comfortably. The wide, funnel-like shape seems to encourage a bigger, more expansive flame; sitting around it felt more like a bonfire than simply burning wood in a container. After 25 minutes, we still had a substantial fire going. Its lower stature kept our feet warm too.

In a recent development, the biggest downside is ash removal. The pan in the base is relatively shallow, and the wide fire pit is awkward to twist and lift off for cleaning. You’ll want long arms—or a second person—to do it comfortably. The stainless-steel finish also turned a light bronze after just one use. A cover costs extra.

Before lighting a single fire, we evaluated the things that can make or break a smokeless fire pit before you ever use them. We assessed the packaging and how well each pit was protected in transit, weighed every model, and evaluated assembly. We read the instructions, noting whether they were clear, complete, and actually useful.

Industry observers note that we considered whether it could be disassembled for storage, and what came in the box versus what required an additional purchase. While We had plenty of outdoor space to work with, safety always came first: we set every pit on heavy-duty pavers and kept a fire extinguisher close at hand.

According to recent reports, then we lit them up. We used comparable loads of seasoned firewood to assess how easily each pit started, how much smoke it produced, how evenly it burned, and how much heat it put out. We paid attention to flame height and consistency, too, and whether the fire actually warmed people sitting around it—not just looked good from a distance. We measured logs to see exactly what each pit could accommodate and tested wood pellets where models supported them.

Finally, we evaluated the less glamorous but equally important details: how easy each pit was to tend, how much ash accumulated, how easily that ash could be removed, and what it took to clean and put each model away. And because a fire pit can be beautiful at 7 p.m. and a pain in the ass at 10 p.m., we tested for both.

Whether you want a smokeless fire pit to heat your outdoor space or be more of an ambient seasonal moment is an crucial consideration. For long nights by the fire with family and friends, you’ll likely want to invest in a larger model that measures 24 inches in diameter. In testing, models that size and up exuded warmth for several feet, and could easily warm four to six people.

According to recent reports, they could also handle 14- to 16-inch-long logs. The trade-off: Models this size are a lot heavier and harder to move. If you’re looking for more of a warming accent, narrower fire pits work wonders. You can also maximize some models’ output by adding a heat deflector that sits above the flames and pushes heat out laterally, instead of letting it escape upward.

Recent findings suggest that ideally, the smokeless fire pit should work right out of the box, with limited-to-no setup, besides setting the pit on a base. It should also break down easily. If you’ll be storing it between fires or seasons, a model that’s easy to disassemble, carry, and put away is key.

The shallower and wider the smokeless fire pit, the easier it is to make a fire from scratch. You simply have more base room to work with to set up your paper, kindling, and wood, and less depth to maneuver to light your fire once ready. No matter your choice, you’ll definitely want a lighter with a long metal wand and a safety catch. None of the models we tested included one.

Burning pellets instead of wood was the closest we got to a truly smokeless fire during our testing. Made of compressed wood waste like sawdust, chips, and shavings, pellets are easy to light, always bone dry, and produce a hotter, more consistent flame than logs. There are trade-offs, though: They lack the classic crackle and pop of a wood-burning fire and that wonderful smell.

Bags of the stuff also typically cost more than a handful of logs at the hardware store, yet burn about the same length of time. But, if you’re allergic to smoke, don’t want your sweaters to smell of it, have wet wood drying out, or want a reliable and even fire every single time, pellets are an excellent way to go. Some fire pits work with them right out of the box; others need an adapter.

Every smokeless pit burns wood. Many smokeless fire pits can also use wood pellets right out of the box. Some, like Solo Stove, need an adapter, so the tiny pellets don’t drop right through the pit’s air holes into the ashcan below. Some portable options may only be wide or deep enough to handle twigs (pellets may be a better option for those).

Pro tip: Wet or green wood will always be slow to burn and emit a lot of smoke; use a moisture meter to suss out whether your logs are dry enough to light up before putting a match to them.

According to recent reports, if you initiative to use your fire pit regularly, easy ash removal should be a deciding factor. The last thing you want to have to do is pick up and tip a heavy steel drum over a trashcan in order to empty it of ash. Instead, look for a removable ash pan or tray that allows you to lift the ash out cleanly once the pit has fully cooled (usually 12 to 24 hours after a fire has ended). Otherwise, you’ll need a shovel to scoop out the ash.

If you don’t have space to leave your fire pit outside all year, think about who will move it and how often. Even a small pit designed for camping trips can weigh as much as 20 pounds. Fortunately, these options usually come with a carrying bag, so you can sling them over your shoulder. Meanwhile, larger models can top 45 pounds (the 24-inch Breeo weighs just over 60 pounds), which matters when you have to move it under cover or into the garage at the end of the season. Units that come apart make this easier; having a dolly or hand truck on hand helps, too.

It has been revealed that material affects how long your newly introduced pit will look the way it does on arrival. While stainless steel looks shiny and modern from the start, heat from the flames will discolor it, and potentially quite swiftly, as some testing demonstrated. (You can restore its original shine with a stainless-steel cleaner such as Bar Keepers Friend, but that’s extra work.) Corten-steel usually costs more but forms a protective rust-colored patina that looks attractively weathered over time. Painted or powder-coated steel usually costs less, but can scratch and chip with repeat use.

Whatever finish you choose, keeping your smokeless fire pit empty of ash and covered when it’s not in use will help extend its life. Rainwater sitting in a fire pit full of ash can create a corrosive, alkaline slurry that accelerates rust and can damage the metal. Some models come with a cover as part of their bundle; others charge extra for it. Our reviews note whether a cover is included in every pick.

It has been revealed that smokeless fire pits can be a lot more than a place to warm your hands on chilly nights. In some cases, you can turn them into an outdoor kitchen. Brands like Breeo, Solo Stove, and Cuisinart have grill grates, griddles, pizza ovens, or roasting sticks that let you cook over an open fire. Other add-ons also make a difference, like a cover, if you initiative to leave it outside when not in use; a spark screen, particularly if you have toddlers and pets around (though, warning: they can also get hot to the touch); and fire pokers or ashtray lifters, so you don’t get your hands dirty. Definitely check the accessory lineup before you buy your pit; they’re often model-specific. A pair of fire-resistant gloves is always a good investment.

Industry observers note that while product photos often depict smokeless fire pits sitting on wood decks or backyards, it’s worth noting that their bases can get hot enough to scorch or discolor lawns, wood decks, composite, and asphalt. Ideally, yours should sit on brick, concrete, stone, or sand. But in the absence of that, a dedicated base (sometimes included, other times sold separately) helps raise the unit off the ground. For an even safer setup, consider adding a fireproof mat underneath. You should also keep a bucket of water or a fire extinguisher nearby and check for local burn bans before lighting. For more on fire pit safety, check out our story.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer.
  • Sources indicate that A judge mentioned he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer. Few details have emerged so far about the government’s search of her home earlier this fall. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Sources indicate that A judge mentioned he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., which included a search of her Washington house last month.

Judge James Boasberg for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search. Boasberg ordered the government to provide him by Friday what could be disclosed in the case. He pointed to how investigators are handling the “speech or debate” clause immunity that Omar has as a sitting member of Congress.

“This is purely legal questions, interesting questions, about the privilege, the extent of the privilege and how it would apply,” Boasberg said.

The Constitution includes an immunity for members of Congress for the “speech or debate” they engage in as part of their jobs.

Recent findings suggest that boasberg also directed the government to propose redactions to the as-yet secret docket. While he stated next week’s expected disclosures would not include the 67-page document that investigators provided to justify the search, he left the door open to unsealing that down the road if the government closes the case or brings charges.

Justice Department attorney Alessandra Serano argued against broad disclosures, calling it “very rare that a precharging, pre-indictment unsealing would happen.”.

The high-profile nature of the investigation leaked into the courtroom Tuesday, as Boasberg cited statements by President Donald Trump and others about the investigation into Omar.

“You have had administration officials, prominent ones, talking about the purpose of the investigation,” Boasberg remarked.

Administration officials have accused Omar of committing immigration crimes for years, and Trump noted last month the DOJ was looking into Omar “strongly.” Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on a recent podcast that investigators had served multiple search warrants and were investigating possible immigration fraud tied to when Omar entered the United States as a child.

Separately, Boasberg stated he may issue rulings in the coming weeks unsealing portions of other court cases tied to the investigation, including one brought by Omar herself earlier this month seeking the return of the items seized in the search.

It has been revealed that the administration executed the search warrant in October, just a few weeks before the midterm elections. The timing of the search drew accusations of political bias from Democrats who claimed that the administration brought the case to sway the midterm elections.

For years Trump has remarked he wanted criminal charges to be brought against his political foes, including Omar and others in Congress.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Riviera Travel River Cruise has declared a C-suite shift as it prepares for another year of anticipated growth.

Travel industry veteran Vicky Billing has been named president of North America, and Stuart Milan has been elevated to chief commercial officer.

According to recent reports, the firm stated in a press release that, bringing 30 years of travel industry experience to her newly introduced role, Billing will oversee Riviera Travel River Cruises’ continued expansion across the U.S. and Canada.

She joins the firm’s multinational executive team, reporting directly to CEO Matt Luscombe, and will oversee all aspects of the company’s North American operations.

Billing succeeds Stuart Milan, who has led Riviera Travel River Cruises’ North American operations for the past three years and will return to the UK, promoted to chief commercial officer.

In his newly introduced role, Milan will lead Riviera Travel River Cruises’ commercial strategy, driving profitable customer growth across revenue management, commercial planning, trade, loyalty, CRM and digital commerce.

“North America is a key part of Riviera Travel River Cruises’ future, and we have significant ambitions for the market,” mentioned Luscombe.

“Billing is an exceptional commercial leader with a real passion for the travel trade, and I have every confidence she’ll build on the momentum already established and help take our North American business to fresh heights.”.

Billing presently serves as Riviera Travel River Cruises’ director of trade, partnerships and loyalty, where she oversees key elements of the company’s commercial strategy across the UK and Ireland.

“I’m thrilled to take on this opportunity and work alongside our team and partners as we build the next chapter of Riviera’s business in North America,” mentioned Billing.

“I’m incredibly proud of what the North American team has built over the last three years,” stated Milan. “We’ve established a strong foundation for continued growth, supported by a brilliant team and increasingly strong relationships across the travel advisor community.”.

The press release added that the appointments of Billing and Milan are part of a broader evolution of Riviera Travel River Cruises’ executive leadership team.

Will Sarson, at the moment product director, has been promoted to chief brand and product officer, overseeing the manufacturer’s brand, product portfolio and guest proposition.

Robin Shaw, at the moment chief commercial officer, will transition to chief transformation officer, overseeing key strategic initiatives with an immediate focus on the future development of Riviera’s river cruise fleet.

All changes are effective beginning April 1, 2027. Existing advisor relationships, sales contacts, and trade programs will remain in place throughout the leadership transition.

Industry News: Australia’s legless geckos evolved like snakes did

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

Industry observers note that australia’s limbless geckos look a lot like snakes. It turns out they’ve evolved like snakes too.

According to recent reports, snakes are technically a highly modified group of legless lizards. Dozens of other lizard lineages have independently lost their legs, too. But the legless pygopod geckos aren’t quite like their slithering nonsnake kin. Pygopods have dietary pickiness and physical diversity patterns that are more reminiscent of those found in snakes than in other legless lizards, researchers report in a preprint posted at bioRxiv.org on October 23.

The 50 recognized species of pygopod geckos are found throughout Australia and New Guinea. Pygopods range from a meter long to the size of half a cooked spaghetti noodle. They have odd tails, which in some species can be fantastically long, exceeding 400 percent of their less-than-1-centimeter-long bodies. Some use their tails like a spring to leap.

“They create a little sine wave and they shoot themselves up in the air, and they can do successive jumps,” says Ian Brennan, an evolutionary biologist at the Queensland Museum Kurilpa in Brisbane, Australia.

But not much else is known about them, Brennan claims.

Recent findings suggest that “They’re real oddballs,” he says, noting that geckos are typically thought of as skilled climbers on walls or glass surfaces. “[Pygopods are] a group that’s gone the exact opposite direction.”.

In a recent development, as part of a large project tackling the genetics of Australia’s lizards and snakes, Brennan and his colleagues gathered data on pygopods’ genes, diet and physical features. They analyzed DNA from all 50 species of pygopod and generated an evolutionary tree. The team also put together data from the literature on the ratio of their body and tail lengths and compared this with a dataset of similar information on over 3,100 lizard and snake species.

Sources indicate that as they evolved, snakes got longer by lengthening their bodies. Limbed lizards tend to get longer by lengthening their tails. The team found that pygopods have done both, an unusual strategy among legless lizards. This dual strategy resulted in some unexpected physical diversity in tail and body ratio.

According to recent reports, next, the team tackled diet, comparing between 1,738 lizard and snake species. Snakes as a group have a broad diet with lots of specialization, which might be partly why they’ve been so successful at diversifying into so many ecological roles in so many habitats, Brennan says. There are pythons that eat only large mammals and sea snakes that eat only fish eggs, for instance.

This pattern is rare in lizards. Most geckos eat insects such as beetles and cockroaches, Brennan indicates. This is especially true of the legless groups, which mostly gobble down whatever insects they happen to slither past.

But the team found that the wide variety in what pygopods as a group will eat is exceeded among reptiles only by monitor lizards and colubrid snakes, a hyperdiverse group of over 2,000 snake species. Within that broad dietary range, particular pygopods flirt with snakelike pickiness. Some pygopods chiefly hunt spiders and scorpions. Another group targets ants and termites. One predatory pygopod — the Lialis genus — gulps down other lizards snake-style.

Pygopods’ evolutionary history may provide hints about how this heightened diversity developed. The team’s findings suggest they split off from other geckos in Australia 50 million years ago — much more recently than when the first snakes evolved around 160 million years ago, but before any modern snake groups reached Australia. Brennan thinks pygopods filled the roles of small snakes on the continent for millions of years in isolation.

Recent findings suggest that “Pygopods were probably on a trajectory to do something spectacular, like snakes,” notes Brennan. “But then all of these [snake] groups indicated up in Australia and filled into those niches.”.

Sonal Singhal — an evolutionary biologist at California State University, Dominguez Hills in Carson — would like to see this study’s data combined with data on pygopods’ skull shape, their habitat use and how their bodies move.

“For example, Lialis can swallow prey whole because their jaws are so flexible and kinetic and their teeth hinge back and forth, allowing them to trap prey.”.

For Brennan, a lesson from the findings is that lacking limbs need not be an evolutionary constraint. Both snakes and pygopods “have diversified to do really interesting things, either due to or in spite of being limbless,” he says.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Viking has taken delivery of the Viking Libra, its newest ocean ship, at Fincantieri’s shipyard in Ancona, Italy.

The 998-guest ship will sail itineraries in the Mediterranean and Northern Europe in her inaugural season.

She is a sister to the rest of Viking’s ocean fleet, but unlike the others she has a hybrid propulsion system designed to run on liquefied hydrogen and fuel cells.

The firm’s next ocean ship, the Viking Astrea, is under construction and will have the same system. Viking expects both ships to be operating on hydrogen in 2027.

“The delivery of the Viking Libra is a proud moment for Viking and an important milestone in our growing ocean fleet,” noted Leah Talactac, president and CEO of Viking.

“Together with the Viking Astrea, she will set a newly introduced standard for innovation as we bring this technology into operation in 2027 and will allow us to welcome even more curious travelers to explore the world in Viking comfort,” she added.

Under its committed orderbook, Viking expects to take delivery of 25 more river ships by 2030, 10 more ocean ships by 2032 and two more expedition ships by 2031.

Those deliveries would bring the company’s fleet to 123 river ships in 2030 and 28 ocean and expedition ships in 2032.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that smartphones may give us an easy access to a light source, but for seeing objects at a distance or brightening a workspace in places like the attic or under the sink, you need the power and range of a LED (light-emitting diode) flashlight.
  • We’ve tested a variety of popular models to find the best flashlights, whether you’re looking for one to use in the midst of a blackout or simply want to put a decent one in the glove box of your car, just in case.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that smartphones may give us an easy access to a light source, but for seeing objects at a distance or brightening a workspace in places like the attic or under the sink, you need the power and range of a LED (light-emitting diode) flashlight. Flashlights are vital for navigating the outdoors at night and absolutely essential during a blackout or emergency, when you don’t want to drain your phone’s battery.

We’ve tested a variety of popular models to find the best flashlights, whether you’re looking for one to use in the midst of a blackout or simply want to put a decent one in the glove box of your car, just in case.

According to recent reports, perhaps the most important element of testing flashlights is to ensure they’re as bright as manufacturers claim. Brands typically list a lumen count, though they’re often inflated. Flashlights tend to dim slightly after you turn them on and your eyes adjust, and how promptly they do so is key. It’s not just about the peak brightness, but how long that brightness actually lasts and how bright the light is after it dims.

To measure lumen, you need an integrating sphere, which is an expensive piece of equipment. So for testing flashlights, we built our own. We consulted with product engineers at two different companies to go over our aims. We also used their commercial spheres to verify lumens on calibration lights to make sure that our own sphere sensors would be accurate.

It has been revealed that after construction and calibration, we measured each flashlight individually at specific time intervals. We recorded our measurements immediately after turning on the light, every 30 seconds for the first 3 minutes, at 5 minutes, and then every 5 minutes for a full half an hour. Our official figure is based on our measurement at 30 seconds because most flashlights drop brightness promptly after that before eventually stabilizing at a dimmer level.

After completing the quantitative portion of our testing process, we used each flashlight in a variety of real-world applications, noting aspects including quality of build, ergonomics, weight, water-resistance, and other key specs.

Our best overall is an evolution on the classic hefty Maglite you remember in your parents junk drawer that could blind you if you looked directly at it. This model trades in the D batteries for a rechargeable and replaceable battery. Furthermore, the flashlight has an LED bulb that shines just as brightly as the old-school models you remember.

While Maglite lists that the flashlight shines with a brightness of 1,082 lumens, our own testing measured an even higher figure, not dropping below 1,082 lumens for more than three minutes.

Beyond this, I really love how it feels in my hand. It isn’t quite as clunky as the giant models of the past, but it still boasts a similar heft that feels solid and durable. The aluminum frame and IPX4 water resistance rating backs that feeling up.

If raw lumens and longevity are top of your priority list, it’s hard to find a better choice than the Streamlight Polytac X USB. The starting point of 554 lumens is already solid, but in testing, the flashlight settles between 334 and 324 lumens, which is a far higher than nearly all other options we tested.

Sources indicate that the relatively compact design doesn’t detract from the overall performance, as the light beam extends for close to 300 feet. That stated, the reflector is not adjustable, so you’ll have to look elsewhere for a floodlight.

Beyond this, we liked the nylon polymer body which was grippy and a lot more comfortable to hold in comparison to a fully metal exterior, which can be icy to the touch in cold temperatures.

There are three preprogrammed function sets we were able to access using Streamlight’s Ten-Tap selector switch. The selection process is a little awkward, but most people will likely only use it sparingly to set the preferred programs, which include low/medium/high, high/strobe/low, and high only. We recommend reading the instructions thoroughly to get this right.

From a fully charged state, the Polytac X ran for almost 5.5 hours during our runtime test before going dark.

No, Energizer isn’t just for batteries and Jeep isn’t just for cars. The collaboration between the two brands has led to an affordable, sturdy flashlight with enough brightness to cut through the darkness during late nights on the trails or on the roadside.

While Jeep’s involvement isn’t more than some design elements and a logo, this particular option is part of a larger lighting collection the brand did in collaboration with Energizer, featuring headlamps and other flashlights.

Sources indicate that during our lumen testing, the flashlight measured a little less than 20 percent below the 1,000 lumens Energizer claims, which isn’t uncommon given nearly all flashlights fall a little short of their advertised number. It still offers tremendous light, especially in tandem with the reflector and lens, which do a nice job angling the light out in a steady, powerful beam.

Test Editor Bradley Ford noted: “The unique feature on this light is the Power Indicator screen for which it is named. When the light is turned on, or the mode changed, the screen displays estimated runtime for that mode—then it switches to battery capacity, listed as charge capacity remaining. Really a nice feature, and better than typical three or four battery-level indicators that are more common.”.

In a recent development, we’ve tested other flashlights from ThruNite and were impressed by their durable, powerful lighting. That’s why we called in the Archer 2A V3 to test.

Industry observers note that the flashlight is said to have more than 8 hours of consistent lumen output, higher than many flashlights we tested. Along with brightness, the Archer flashlight is compact and easy to carry around for everyday tasks. Need a quick light to check the back of your shed? Simply reach into your pocket and use the Archer.

Recent findings suggest that the ThruNite won’t be top of the list in any one category but thrives on being pretty consistent across all of them. It’s bright, long-lasting, and durable, which is just about all you really need.

This ArkPro line of flashlights from Olight caught our eye not just for its slim, pocket-sized design, but also for the volume of additional features it offers. The ArkPro Ultra has four different lighting options: a long-range spotlight, a shallow floodlight, a UV light, and a laser pointer.

Sources indicate that furthermore, you can use those lights in combination with one another. For example, you can turn the laser pointer on and off while shining the flood.

During testing, the long-range spotlight and floodlight ended up being our favorite dual feature. We were able to illuminate small dark rooms easily with the shallow floodlight, while using the long-range spotlight for hallways and large empty spaces. Having both in one body is not a common feature. While we might have initially winced at the price tag, the Olight makes a solid case that it has the value of multiple flashlights.

According to recent reports, that noted, it’s worth noting that our measured lumens fell short of Olight’s claimed 1,700 figure. The flashlight is still much brighter than most other options but did degrade over the 30-minute test.

Another promising feature: the physical display lights on the body that indicate battery, brightness, and a lockout mode. That last one prevents kids from accidentally flashing the laser or other lights in their eyes by locking the device from shutting on and off.

Sources indicate that the USB-C charging is also a plus. With nearly every smartphone charger already built in the same design, you’ve likely got dozens of compatible charging cords lying around.

Full Olight ArkPro Ultra Review.

This small, tactical flashlight from ThruNite does a number of key things well. The over 2400 lumens at its brightest setting rivals some of the most powerful options we recommend. At the same time the compact body and hip clip make it a great portable option that easily slips in a pocket or center console of your car.

What sets the TC15 apart from other options is the extraordinary runtime. On its Firefly mode (which is admittedly a very low setting), the flashlight can run for up to 30 days before needing to recharge.

The durable aluminum body is capable of handling a steep drop and the IPX8 rating means you can feel confident using it in the rain.

Traditional light bulbs, while nostalgic, are inefficient and waste a lot of energy. According to the U.S. Department of Energy, as much as 90 percent of the energy required to illuminate an incandescent light is given off—essentially lost—as heat. Halogen bulbs are an improvement on classic incandescent lights, but still generate a ton of heat. Beyond this, the bulbs themselves are also quite delicate. If dropped, they can easily shatter.

Industry observers note that in contrast, LEDs are 70 to 75 percent more efficient than incandescent lights. That efficiency doesn’t lead to lower brightness either, with LEDs actually shining far stronger than most classic bulbs. The LED itself is a semiconductor that emits light when current passes through it. Furthermore, without a delicate filament inside, LEDs are far more durable.

While LEDs in flashlights are more efficient than traditional bulbs, they still generate a fair amount of heat. Especially as brands continue to push to create brighter and brighter flashlights, the heat generated grows too. That mentioned, most LED flashlights have circuitry designed to manage power consumption and prevent your light from burning up.

Sources indicate that for the most part, as long as you use common sense and don’t max out your light for hours on end, your LED flashlight should be fine. Take care of it responsibly and you’ll never deal with heat problems.

It has been revealed that the actual brightness of your flashlight is measured in lumens. Lumens are essentially measuring the total light created by flashlight, with the higher the figure, the brighter the flashlight should shine.

Recent findings suggest that even accurate figures reported by a firm can often refer to the absolute highest possible lumen output, which is not realistically what you end up using most of the time. Being able to measure them ourselves provides a lot of much needed reassurance.

Sources indicate that that said, lumens aren’t the end all, be all. A lot of the perceived brightness and clarity of the beam is due to the reflector shape and lens. So, the width and length of the light beam from your flashlight will likely be a better determination of whether it works for you or not.

Industry observers note that IP is short for ingress protection, meaning protection from stuff getting inside the flashlight. Those letters will be followed by two numbers: The first digit indicates protection from solids like dust or grit. The second digit indicates protection from moisture, in this case the concern is usually water. Sometimes there will be an “X” in place of one of those numbers, which means the flashlight hasn’t been tested for protection from solids (if the X is where the first number should be) or liquids (if it’s where the second should be).

Industry observers note that for the first number, protection from solids, the highest rating, 6, indicates the light should be impenetrable by dust and sand. The highest value for the second number, representing protection from liquid, is 8. The flashlight can be submerged in water deeper than 1 meter for longer than 30 minutes, with no harmful effects.

It has been revealed that A flashlight’s IP rating gives a partial picture of its durability. You’ll also want to take into account things like the materials used—ranging from lightweight but less-than-durable plastic to rubberized enclosures to heavy-duty anodized aluminum—and whether the flashlight floats in water in addition to being waterproof, not to mention the warranty.

As our first-hand testing showed, manufacturer estimates for flashlight specs are relatively accurate, especially regarding the peak brightness. It’s key to keep in mind that there are a variety of factors that can influence a flashlight’s moment-to-moment performance, such as its battery life and how long it has run in the past few hours.

Industry observers note that as we mentioned, it is normal for flashlights to only shine at peak brightness for a few minutes before sliding back to the middle of their range. The good news is your visibility won’t suffer for that.

It has been revealed that that depends on how you’re using your flashlight. Manufacturer Nitecore suggests a range of 1 to 300 lumens should be enough to light up a room or an intermittently lit outdoor area. Look for 300 to 980 lumens for walking in the dark without any additional light sources. Mechanics and other workers who need to see precise details in complete darkness might go a little higher, say 1,000 to 1,300 lumens.

In a recent development, hunters or law enforcement might use brighter flashlights than that, but it really depends on the task. Furthermore, it’s important to remember that powerful flashlights can be disruptive to other people and wildlife, so choose your light carefully.

Recent findings suggest that flashlight enthusiasts often recommend making a flash part of your “everyday carry,” keeping it on you at all times as you would with your keys or smartphone. Personally, we recommend being proactive and keeping it around whenever or wherever you think there’s a chance you may need some extra light. For example, if you’re going on a hiking trip or evening walk, it’s a no-brainer.

It has been revealed that it’s never a bad idea to stash a flashlight on each floor of your home in case of a power outage or other emergency. That way, you can easily grab it without going up or down stairs in the dark. It’s best to keep them in a place that you know you’ll remember and is easy to find in the dark, such as a small drawer.

We also stronglyrecommend keeping a flashlight in your car, as you never know when you might have a mechanical glitch at night, and you’ll want to save your phone battery.

Separately, FEMA and The Department of Homeland Security recommend that you keep an emergency kit with a flashlight and other essentials in a cool, dry place somewhere at home, as well as in your car. In order to keep the kit intact and ready for an emergency, the flashlight in your emergency kit should be a backup, not your primary flashlight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep.-elect Chris Rabb, D-Pa., greets current members of Congress in the Capitol on Nov. 11. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

When Rep.-elect Chris Rabb first worked on Capitol Hill in the 1990s, it didn’t exactly inspire him to want to go into politics.

“I remarked, ‘Oh, this is how the sausage is made? I should be a vegan,’” the Pennsylvania Democrat recalled.

Working for Carol Moseley Braun, the first Black woman elected as a U.S. senator, Rabb saw threats and “just vile things” directed at her.

“My entrée to service behind the scenes was seeing voluminous amounts of violence, hate speech and death threats against my boss, and I thought to myself, ‘Why would anyone want to serve?’” he noted.

Recent findings suggest that during his time in the state legislature starting in 2017, Rabb “fell in love with public service, despite the vitriol.” Now, the democratic socialist describes coming to Congress as “surreal,” as he succeeds retiring Rep. Dwight Evans in a deep-blue district based in West Philadelphia.

Rabb is one of more than a dozen incoming members who have worked on the Hill before, ranging from interns to chiefs of staff and everything in between.

Unlike some in the 100-plus-strong freshman class, they already know their way around the hallways. And Rabb has some advice for his fresh colleagues: “Treat your staff well. Take care of your staff; they’ll take care of you.”.

Here are some of the former staffers who will join the House in January.

In a recent development, A couple years ago, Killin was working as chief of staff to former second gentleman Doug Emhoff. But she started out on the Hill.

“It is helpful to know, as I joke, where the bathrooms are, but I still feel like I have a lot to learn,” remarked the Army veteran, who unseated Republican Rep. Jeff Crank in a Colorado Springs-area district.

She served as the top staffer for three House Democrats: Donna Shalala of Florida, Carolyn Maloney of Newly introduced York and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington.

“I’ve actually opened up two freshman offices, so it’s helpful to have done that before,” Killin noted.

Recent findings suggest that white will be just the third person in modern times to hold the job of nonvoting D.C. delegate. He replaces retiring Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton — also his former boss.

Recent findings suggest that before his time on the D.C. Council, he worked as her legislative counsel, watching her navigate a role with limited power in her perennial fight for statehood.

“I need to make sure I’m developing a national profile for this seat,” he said, vowing to continue the quest for full representation even as President Donald Trump seeks to exert more control over the District.

One of just a few Republican women in the freshman class, Gruters said she “never in a million years” imagined coming to Congress herself, despite her years as a staffer.

She will replace retiring Rep. Vern Buchanan in Florida’s 16th District, after once serving as his operations director. She also worked as district director for Rep. Greg Steube, R-Fla.

“I never thought this would be the path, but I’m honored to do it,” said Gruters, whose husband leads the Republican National Committee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Carnival Cruise Line is expanding its onboard beverage packages to two of its private destinations: Celebration Key and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay.

According to a recent press release, passengers will be able to order drinks included in their packages at the destinations starting in February 2027.

The extension will be available for Carnival’s CHEERS!, CHEERS! Zero Proof™, Bottomless Bubbles™ and CHEERS! Social drink packages.

Carnival noted the move will “give guests who purchase these packages greater value for their vacation dollars.”.

The change brings Carnival closer to other cruise lines that already extend their beverage packages to private islands.

While some brands, including Norwegian Cruise Line and MSC Cruises, limit the land extension to their premium packages, others include all packages.

In related news, Carnival also announced the first details of the fresh Carnival Destiny, which will enter service in 2029, as well as an order for two smaller newbuilds.

The firm is also investing in Paradise Collection, its portfolio of private destinations across the Caribbean and the Bahamas.

Celebration Key will see the biggest investment, with a significant expansion project set to take place over the next few years.

The private destination in Grand Bahama will see its daily capacity increased by 6,000 guests, with the expansion divided into two phases.

The first will be ready in 2028 and will feature a heated, beach-entry pool with a swim-up bar, as well as six waterslides, a dry climbing structure and a drenching bucket for children.

In 2030, the second phase will add a major water park with 18 waterslides, a lazy river with float-up bars and swim-in/swim-out cabanas, as well as a new exclusive area with an infinity pool, more beach access and new dining and bar concepts.

Carnival noted that, with six exclusive destinations in five countries, its lineup is the largest in the industry.

A cosmically close supernova may spill the stellar explosion’s secrets

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is a human-written story voiced by AI.
  • When astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day.
  • “I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” says astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

When astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day. But scientists soon realized this one was something very special, and they’ve been hustling to study it ever since.

“I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” says astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University.

Industry observers note that soon after scientists spotted the explosion on November 2, they determined it hadn’t yet peaked in brightness, giving scientists an early glimpse at the event. Even more thrilling, within a day of the explosion’s discovery, astronomers had classified it as a type Ia supernova. These particular outbursts are rare, but they’re astronomical superstars: Scientists use their trademark explosion pattern as a “standard candle” to measure distance into the universe — most notably to discover that the universe’s expansion is accelerating. And to round out a trifecta of reasons to be excited, these blasts rarely occur so close to Earth.

Industry observers note that astronomers know type 1a supernovas occur upon the reignition and resulting self-destruction of a white dwarf star, the small cool remnants of a star like the sun that’s too small to become a superdense neutron star or black hole at its demise. Scientists also know that powering back on requires reaching about 1.44 times the mass of the sun, which can occur only if something is giving the white dwarf extra mass.

But scientists aren’t sure what that something is — whether these supernovas are triggered by a second white dwarf or some sort of star that’s still burning. Usually, these explosions occur so far away that astronomers can’t get a good look at where they come from. But SN 2026ahvu is perhaps 50 million light-years or less away from Earth.

“They happen so rarely at this distance that it could hopefully help us figure out why this white dwarf exploded in the first place,” says astronomer Yvette Cendes of the University of Oregon in Eugene, who has been arranging for radio telescopes to observe the outburst.

Sarbadhicary and colleagues have already submitted preliminary findings November 6 at arXiv.org suggesting that the former white dwarf was less than 100 million years old. That’s remarkably young compared with other supernovas of this type, and may help scientists finetune their understanding of these outbursts.

“These explosions have been enduring mysteries for us for decades, and whenever something happens this close, it’s just really exciting,” Sarbadhicary indicates.
