Global Airlines Is “Fyre Festival”, Not Virgin Atlantic

📅 16 May 2025 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1635 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Godsavethepoints

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday, a Hi-Fly charter airplane took off from Glasgow bound for New York, with Hi-Fly crews and pilots.
  • Recent findings suggest that in 2025, crazy things are par for the course, so that didn’t stop all sorts of promising headlines of a revolution in the skies.
  • In reality, anyone can charter a plane and have Hi-Fly operate it, and anyone foolish enough can pay extra for a custom paint job with their logo, or more financially insane — buy a scrapyard A380 and be on the hook for its maintenance, while paying a third party to fly it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, a Hi-Fly charter airplane took off from Glasgow bound for New York, with Hi-Fly crews and pilots. If you read the papers, it was purportedly ‘Global Airlines’ maiden flight, even though there’s no regularly scheduled service, the pilots and crew weren’t theirs, they couldn’t legally sell airline tickets on their own website and they don’t have a license to operate.

Recent findings suggest that in 2025, crazy things are par for the course, so that didn’t stop all sorts of promising headlines of a revolution in the skies. This is the airline that promised stunning innovation and joy in the air, and the press gave Global Airlines an early gift, by comparing the story to Richard Branson and Virgin Atlantic. That’s just insane, as you’ll soon read.

In reality, anyone can charter a plane and have Hi-Fly operate it, and anyone foolish enough can pay extra for a custom paint job with their logo, or more financially insane — buy a scrapyard A380 and be on the hook for its maintenance, while paying a third party to fly it.

In a recent development, the whole ‘Global’ pitch was that people love the Airbus A380, hate all the current global airline experiences ( really?) and airline services — and a revolution in the skies, can happen again. It sounded exciting. We all like to dream. Global’s first flight would be the testament to what air travel can be and something passengers love. So, how’d they do?

When Virgin Atlantic launched in 1984, the airline industry had been in a massively “beige” management consultant style, joy killer phase for a decade.

The fun “golden era” aircraft spaces and frills of the 60’s had largely been stripped out and bus travel comparisons were totally fair. Richard Branson’s light hearted approach to service and differentiated selling could shift dollars and votes — and measurably did.

Recent findings suggest that let me be very clear: that simplicity in differentiation is no longer the case. You cannot shift wallets and put butts in seats just by saying you have a cool airplane alone, or a bar on board (particularly when it’s just a beverage cart that says pub).

From leading (actually real) global airlines, passengers expect, at minimum, the following….

When “Global”, and by Global I really do legally, technically mean Hi-Fly the jet charter firm which actually flew the scrapyard plane that “Global” bought, they did NOT have….

Recent findings suggest that travel blogger Noel Phillips shared some of the trip with his following. The following screen grabs are…. cute?

According to recent reports, the truth is, Virgin Atlantic didn’t have nearly as gargantuan of a task in the 80’s as any airline coming to market does today. In the 80’s many airlines were stuck, did lack innovation and had a pool of largely uninspired talent, with no experience outside of the airline vertical. There also wasn’t this whole technology thing, as standard expectation.

It has been revealed that that’s all so far from the case these days and most that are specialized in the airline world are wickedly sharp. Most newly introduced people I know at airlines now also come from major tech companies, other travel verticals or impactful innovation firms.

Airlines are getting pretty good at this ole’ air travel thing.

A differentiated approach to smiles on board and a little bit of extra focus on fun, food and drinks could really shift minds and mentalities in the 1980’s, but now you gotta back it up, baby.

Everyone likes to feel special and Virgin, forever, has made people feel special at a time without tech. I’d argue Virgin has taught Delta a lot about that, and it’s a contributing factor to Delta’s rise as a premium airline. It didn’t happen overnight, and what looks easy never is.

Getting people to fly with you is now about safety, reliability, excellence in mobile technology, schedule and personalization. Then fine, we can care about which champagne; or caterer or lounge style or airport, and which celebs like it. Yes, these legacy airlines can appear stuffy at times, but my god, can you not marvel at the technology revolution making air travel journeys excellent?

Sources indicate that on real airlines, before I even arrive at the airport, I can use the NFC chip in my passport pressed against my phone to validate my document and bypass human interaction. I board a United, or any serious airline flight nowadays and see a notification that my bag is loaded onto a cart to be loaded on the plane, then again when it’s loaded onto the plane!

It has been revealed that I hit the wifi and I’m connected sitting at the gate. If for some reason the flight is at all delayed, or connection in jeopardy, I can instantly rebook onto any other service at no charge, without talking to a soul, with just a tap on the app.

Their seag back screens have blockbuster movies, boxsets and everything else you could want for a one hour, or 15 hour journey. It’s all just standard now, not innovative.

In a recent development, the app navigates me through the airport and even tells me when my zone is boarding. AKA – stand the “f” back. The food is at least solid, the beverages are getting better because of their scale (buying power) and there are fewer poor customer service interactions because of how tech forward and seamless journeys are.

Industry observers note that all the great, big airlines do this. This is like… baseline for a real player.

Tell me, or ask the Global Airlines CEO, James Asquith, where in the roadmap all of these essentials are? I want to make it clear that their priority for the last three years was a Soho House press conference about serving champagne in economy, maybe, “if they could get the economics right” rather than any of these basic things.

Recent findings suggest that and in the end, they didn’t even deliver on the silly things they prioritized. The first Global flight wasn’t a remotely differentiated take on economy, business or first, as promised. It was 12 year old seats from another lackluster airline, without real refurb and even the long haul dignity of any seat back entertainment, which that airline which scrapped the plane offered.

Industry observers note that if Richard Branson was at the helm, they never would’ve let that flight take off. Making a splash means at least doing one thing differently, right? An airline promising total innovation, A380 experience and differentiation cannot launch a flight which does not even meet the basic standards of budget carriers like Norse. You just can’t take off. You innovative something!

Let’s not forget that when Richard Branson formed Virgin Atlantic, he’d already founded a notable brand and number of businesses in the UK, was quite famous, and filed records and company books in a place where they are scrutinized. He was “real”, even if some was bluster. The public could and did use his businesses.

James Asquith’s only claim to fame, other than from the Instagram account he bought followers for, to fake fame — yes, factually — is that he was the “CEO” of Holiday Swap. Omg, so big time!

The business purports to be a home swap company, though there are no financial records of any legal merit in the West, and despite my damndest multi-year attempts, no record of actual customers. Simple use of Similar Web or review sites will help your own conclusions. You can read old blog posts for more musings. The rumors of what laundered through are scary. Maybe a real journalist can find out for us?

I actually think it’s dangerous to the public to compare these two people.

According to recent reports, I’ve had the good fortune of meeting Richard Branson many times throughout the years and he’s always been wildly impressive. Wickedly sharp, analytical, funny and personable. It’s easy to put in a good shift for PR purposes, but I’ve observed levels of deep dive knowledge that no setup encounter can protect for — and genuine interest too. He cares about his people and he worries about the details.

In a recent development, I also have many people in my personal life connected to the Virgin Atlantic founder and I know of nothing but admiration and respect for the man, his manufacturer ethos and family. Business in the front, party in the back.

My only encounter with James Asquith was when he was fuming that he wasn’t invited on an airlines press trip, slid into my Instagram DM’s wanting me to blast them – and for us to be best buds as we roast a major (actual) global airline. That airline later confidentially told me he was banned from flying, due to his antics. I politely declined and he unfollowed me. It was soooo cool.

I guess if you can’t fly other airlines, you start your own?

In a recent development, so yeah, if you ever feel like putting your life in the hands of an airline without functioning entertainment screens, or WiFi, or regularly scheduled service, or new seats, or a mobile app, or an actual license to fly planes, definitely fly with Global. Oh, and no viable loyalty program either. Forget about earning points from daily spending and turning them into upgrades.

Those other “boring” airlines with all the bells and whistles above are clearly not ready to make travel great, with a newly introduced golden age, again.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This week, Virgin Atlantic celebrates 25 years of flying to India.
  • On the sidelines of the IATA Annual General Meeting, basically the UN General Assembly of airlines, the new strategic partnership for India was confirmed with very interesting nods to the future.
  • IndiGo carries more passengers in India than anyone else and will connect US and UK/European customers flying Virgin, Delta and Air France KLM onward in India, while also helping fill seats for these European and North American partners, as their own customers head West.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week, Virgin Atlantic celebrates 25 years of flying to India. In Virgin fashion, it’s doing so in style, with a joint announcement among partners Delta Airlines, Air France-KLM, and a new strategic partner IndiGo.

On the sidelines of the IATA Annual General Meeting, basically the UN General Assembly of airlines, the new strategic partnership for India was confirmed with very interesting nods to the future.

IndiGo carries more passengers in India than anyone else and will connect US and UK/European customers flying Virgin, Delta and Air France KLM onward in India, while also helping fill seats for these European and North American partners, as their own customers head West.

According to recent reports, that’s probably a good thing, because with recent service additions, Virgin now flies a million seats a year to India and it sounds like others are piling on more flights too. It’s now one of the largest operators to India.

It has been revealed that I’ve been bullish on India as the next great center of the world for a while now. It’s not necessarily that I’m at all intelligent, it’s just based on the fact that India is the world’s largest population. But, when Ed Bastian, Delta’s formidable CEO indicates it, people tend to listen. Bastian mentioned India being the most crucial aviation market globally now and signaled a return of direct services for the carrier as well.

According to recent reports, virgin has been a small step ahead, adding service regularly on their Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore routes. IndiGo chose this alliance over formidable competition and this will certainly be a space to watch as more global airlines and alliances focus on India.

Industry observers note that geo-political activity points to India becoming a fresh manufacturing super power, in addition to its prolific work in tech, IT and customer service, not to mention blossoming tourism. These kind of globally connected businesses are big business, huge in fact, for corporate contracts and easy onward connectivity to regional sites is essential. The partnership makes sense.

It has been revealed that in a somewhat rare and impressive signal of unity and seriousness towards India, Virgin Atlantic made their India crews part of the core Virgin family, rather than as contractors through a third party local company, known in aviation world as a GSA. This means Virgin’s India crews are a part of the full team, with benefits too.

According to recent reports, when asked about loyalty implications of the new alliance, Virgin Atlantic CEO, Shai Weiss, noted a mutual passion for using loyalty to enhance guest experience far beyond just the earn and burn of points and miles. For future iterations, they’ve offered the following….

The MoU (memorandum of understanding) also creates a framework for deeper collaboration between the carriers on a bilateral and multilateral basis; contemplates commercial collaboration including network, loyalty, cargo and sales, subject to regulatory approvals; explores areas of non-commercial cooperation including aircraft maintenance, sustainability, training, ground handling; and acknowledges the need to develop advanced collaboration through use of technology to efficiently service joint customers.

IndiGo will provide onward connectivity for Virgin and the other strategic partners to 32 destinations, making it easier than ever to see Udaipur, Jaipur, Mumbai, Kashmir and delights further south in Bangalore and Goa.

I just returned from the lovely Leela Palace in Delhi, as I watched the news happen live.

In a recent development, to me, India is a country of joy. Even people with truly nothing seem to find positivity and it’s generally a way of life here. Hospitality is as warm and steeped in tradition as it comes, too. It’s hot, it’s humid, but it’s an experience unlike any other and that’s something that’s harder to say these days than I’d like.

Industry observers note that the food, ugh. I adore. Sure, I’ll take a dosa from the South over a heavy curry from the North most days, but I love both and if you don’t love a good black daahl there’s something wrong with you.

It has been revealed that in short, it’s already fairly easy to get to India but it’s about to get a whole lot easier and not just to hub cities too. More seats means more chances to use points, by the way!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that growing up in Fort Lauderdale, the Bahamas always felt like an extension of South Florida to me. Just a short flight or boat ride away, the archipelago was somewhere I returned to often, and still do. Yet what continues to surprise me is how different one island can feel from the next. I've always thought it was a shame that so many visitors to the Bahamas never make it beyond Nassau or Freeport. Eleuthera has some of the prettiest beaches I've seen, the water around the Exumas is almost unbelievably clear, and the Abacos have small waterfront towns that are worth exploring. Each island has its own personality, and even after years of visiting, there are so many I still want to discover.

Industry observers note that renting a home is one of my favorite ways to experience it all. Beautiful beachfront villas, colorful cottages, and contemporary homes with pools overlooking the sea are everywhere in the Bahamas. Having your own place makes it easy to settle in, explore a little, and enjoy the particular rhythm of whichever island you've chosen. After so many visits, I’m eager to step slightly off the typical tourist path (although the resorts and hotels here are also beautiful), and these Bahamas Airbnbs are a great way to do so. Read on for my most-recommended rentals in the Bahamas, from beachfront stays to island cottages.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost and Guest Favorite status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Number of guests: 12 (up to 8 adults and 4 children)Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 4.5 bathsWhy we love it: Heated pool, direct beach access, bohemian interiors.

With its natural textures, airy interiors, and covered outdoor lounge, Corsair Key feels specially designed for long, unhurried days by the water. Four king bedrooms offer plenty of room for families or friends, while a heated swimming pool and direct beach access make it tempting to stay put. The well-equipped kitchen and generous dining spaces are especially appealing for groups who enjoy cooking together. And with a location in Bimini (the westernmost district of The Bahamas) being so close to South Florida, getting here is surprisingly easy.

Location: Rockwell Island, BiminiThings to do nearby: Radio Beach, Bimini snorkeling, fishing excursions.

This five-bedroom bungalow embraces its retro personality with bold artwork, wicker lighting, and colorful bedrooms. Outside, a heated pool is surrounded by tropical landscaping, while Harbour Island's famous pink sands are just a short walk away. It's a playful alternative to more traditional island cottages, with enough room for the whole family; kids will particularly love the bunk beds.

The best feature of this three-bedroom cottage? The uninterrupted sea views, visible through expansive windows and from the waterfront deck. The interiors are simple and contemporary, with an open living space that keeps the focus firmly on the scenery. Inside, you’ll find a private cinema, a fully equipped kitchen, and a separate suite for those who want a bit more privacy. Residents also have access to an infinity pool, a private beach, padel and pickleball courts, and a dock where boats can collect guests for excursions.

The open-proposal living area makes gathering easy, and the bedroom configuration—two kings with oceanfront views, a queen, and a room with a queen and a bunk bed—works well for families traveling together. Kayaks and paddleboards make it easy to explore the bay, while concierge services can arrange everything from a private chef to a day trip exploring the Exuma cays. Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov.
  • Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of issues even as he appears politically weakened at home.
  • According to recent reports, trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Iori Sagisawa / POOL / AFP via Getty Images).

Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of issues even as he appears politically weakened at home.

According to recent reports, trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal. But before he left, Trump signaled the three-way talks also likely would include the artificial intelligence race, Moscow’s bloody war with Ukraine, global trade and his standoff with Iran.

Industry observers note that the U.S. commander in chief’s tendency to sound deferential to Putin and habit of referring to Xi as a personal “friend” concerns many congressional Democrats. But Trump’s GOP allies on Capitol Hill, despite this month’s midterm election losses, still describe him as a dealmaker who has a chance to use his final years to bend Putin and Xi toward U.S. interests.

Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, noted Tuesday he was hopeful that Trump could make some progress on at least one issue with the Russian and Chinese leaders.

“As we all know, China and Russia want to destroy our way of life,” he mentioned. “But it would be great to reduce … nuclear stockpiles and make sure we're not going to ever get attacked.

In a recent development, still, Scott sounded skeptical about two world leaders Trump has tried to keep close during his two terms. “But do I trust Xi or Putin? No, they're a bunch of liars.” Asked if he worries Trump might trust them too much, Scott replied: “I don't think he trusts him any more than I do. … I'm glad the president's trying. Hope springs eternal. But do I actually really believe something good's going to come out of it? I don't.”.

Outgoing House Armed Services Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., said part of Trump’s talks on Thursday “should be to make sure the world is a safer place, to make sure we don't have aggressive behavior like Russia in an unprovoked attack against Ukraine.

“They ought to be talking about how they don't do those sorts of things, how they don't threaten their neighbors, how they don't try to intimidate through the assertion of force that they ought to be able to work together to make sure we assure a safe globe,” said Wittman, who lost his reelection race earlier this month.

That comment came one day after Trump told reporters as he left the White House for Asia that he sees Putin “backing down a little bit” in his conduct of the war with Ukraine.

It has been revealed that “I think he could be tougher. I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump noted Monday. “I think he's backing down.”.

Those kinds of deferential remarks about the Russian leader are a major reason why some Democrats have heartburn about Thursday’s meeting.

According to recent reports, senate Armed Services member Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, said Tuesday that she’s concerned about the Shenzhen summit because “I’m not sure what’s going to pop out of [Trump’s] mouth next — especially for a meeting with two guys he clearly likes.”.

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., also a member of the Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, said he has “high hopes” for the trilateral meeting — but “maybe not high expectations.”.

In a recent development, “I have some points of anxiety. I'm nervous about any discussion about Ukraine that doesn't involve the Ukrainians. And, so, some of the advance to this is like, ‘We're going to talk about ending the Ukraine war.’ You can't do that without Ukraine at the table,” Kaine noted. “So the desire to bring about more peace and stability, that's a good thing to talk about. But no conditions about Ukraine and ending that war without them at the table? Not so sure about that.”.

Industry observers note that during remarks Tuesday on the Senate floor, Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer criticized what he described as Trump’s misplaced priorities.

It has been revealed that “Enforcement of the fresh rules restricting China’s access to our most sensitive AI chips should start today,” the New York Democrat said, adding that Trump should focus more of his Asia swing on securing commitments from U.S. allies to block China from gaining an upper hand in the AI technology race.

Trump touted just that on Tuesday during remarks in Manila at a U.S.-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines.

Sources indicate that “Since I returned to office, we've made major trade deals with Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea, and almost everybody, frankly, at the table,” he said. “And we've made many other vital agreements across the region spanning energy, critical minerals and technology.”.

But on Wednesday, Trump appeared to have pivoted to the trip’s main event.

He stood beside Xi at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and smiled as Putin approached. Trump extended his hand and shook Putin’s as the Chinese leader looked on.

Scott, a Trump ally in the Senate, remarked Tuesday he sees the president “trying to build relationships to try to make sure we don't end up at war [because] he doesn't like war.”.

In a recent development, trump signaled Monday that he might press Xi for details on an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, costing the AI mogul his job as the company’s president and CEO. He also noted he could bring up Nvidia’s sales of sophisticated microchips that many lawmakers — Republican and Democrat — want to ensure remain in the U.S. for domestic AI development.

The administration’s response to the turmoil at Nvidia, with Trump even suggesting he'd support Huang returning as CEO, is a rare area where Republicans have expressed concern publicly. House Energy and Commerce Committee Chair Brett Guthrie, R-Kent., wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday seeking information about “the implementation of federal laws governing technology exports, in particular the application of export controls relating to semiconductor chips, the effect of which has a broad impact on America’s race with China to artificial intelligence (AI) dominance and the ability of U.S. companies to set global technology standards.”.

Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Problems at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote this week that for the three leaders, the “path is fraught with challenges.”.

Industry observers note that “Putin could diplomatically outmaneuver the Trump administration and make any progress on nuclear issues dependent on undermining Western support to Ukraine,” she wrote in an analysis for the Washington, D.C.-based think tank. “Even the optics of Trump and Putin negotiating while the war continues and as Russia ramps up missile strikes on Ukrainian civilian targets could be interpreted as undermining U.S. values.”.

  • And that’s a shame, because there’s been a lovely tourism revolution brewing there, where local hoteliers are bringing back the kind of experience and hospitality that you want to come back for over and over again.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s June, and for perhaps the first time in modern history, Santorini isn’t crowded. Those earthquakes a good few months ago? Not even a flower pot was tipped over, yet incessant clickbait headlines managed to have a lasting impact.

And that’s a shame, because there’s been a lovely tourism revolution brewing there, where local hoteliers are bringing back the kind of experience and hospitality that you want to come back for over and over again.

As someone who goes at least once or twice a year, and will again very shortly, I can only advocate to tick it off the bucket list this summer, because you’ll never find prices, availability or an experience quite like it again for a while.

In a recent development, in the last 20 years, Santorini got totally overrun. Cruise tourism and day trip mania somewhat ruined a once idyllic, low-key fishing island and then Instagram and TikTok lit the match.

But now the TikTok crowd is in Mykonos and Santorini, as unequalled in beauty as ever, is lovely again. Hotels like The Vasilicos and Santorini Sky bring wildly different, delightfully luxurious and hospitality driven experiences to the island.

In a recent development, beach clubs, yes Santorini’s beaches are underrated, have made a nice little mark on quieter coasts with great effect too. Assyrtiko, the local grape has hit the world stage as a darling of sommeliers in top restaurants and vineyards like Vassaltis offer stunning tasting experiences.

And the food? There’s no Nobu, or Scorpios here, so there are plenty of places to feel the benefit of European pricing, including a personal favorite at Kantouni.

Sources indicate that the trouble with Santorini has historically been that many of the best hotels are small, they fill up swiftly, and as they do, they charge a fortune. For the best, like the ones mentioned above, it’s still worth it. But this season, all across the board, prices are lower and even if you don’t care about price, many of the best which might typically be sold out for the season have rooms.

As an additional tailwind for travelers, flights between the US and Europe are quieter this summer, which means there’s deals to be had with both points and cash from major markets to Santorini. If you don’t see cheap flights to Santorini, try a major hub and booking an onward ticket separately.

Naturally, precaution is a good thing in life. But fear mongering for the sake of clicks is another beast and I can’t help but be fairly appalled by the many weeks and months of coverage and follow up coverage, reiterating a narrative of fear… despite no damage to anything, anywhere.

If you do bag a great deal this summer and visit one of my very favorite places, and use this great Santorini guide to make the most of your time, you can thank the media.

There’s no huge unlock of newly introduced places or highly curated places that you could virtually always stamp as worth recommending to a friend, the way you’d rate an Aman, St. Regis, or Four Seasons hotel.

It’s above my pay-grade as a blogger on this topic, but it seems like Wander co-invests in the real estate portfolio’s, or partners with owners in a unique way that’s far more integrated than others.

According to recent reports, most Wander properties are around $1000 a night. Some will be half that, some will be double. On its face, that’s intimidating to many, but when you factor in the number of bedrooms and features it’s really reasonable. Families, or multi-family get togethers… amazing.

According to recent reports, all Wander.com properties are at least two bedrooms and many are four, five or even twelve. One is an entire island with multiple residential complexes. For me, I love these sort of getaways for catching up with family or friends, and I never mind when other people are contributing too.

We’ve had some of our best ever vacations renting a house in Palm Springs for weeks or months at a time. Often, family or friends want in too, so we split the house and end up with two bedrooms each for under $500 per night.

That’s highly competitive in any hotel market for two rooms and the x-factor comes in the form of privacy, full on kitchens, gym facilities, often and a pool or entertainment area and laundry too.

In a recent development, we’ve used these bonus rooms and features to socialize or catch up with people in the serenity of the home, not annoyed by service, crowded pools or tight room setups. For a longer stay, I absolutely hate having to rely on a hotel kitchen for every meal. I love to hit a local market and grill with family or guests.

A problem with one of Delta’s weight-and-balance systems delayed hundreds of flights Sunday, with backups most acute at the nation’s busiest airport.

According to FlightAware, Delta delayed over 2,100 flights Sunday and canceled 274.

Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport was the hardest hit, with about 700 flights delayed, though not all were Delta connections.

Sources indicate that delta mentioned in a statement that its employees were using manual workarounds for baggage processing. It also said it would rebook customers on the next available flight and provide meals and hotel rooms where needed.

In a recent development, the FAA stated on X that the problem was specific to Delta and had nothing to do with the agency’s air traffic control system, which crashed on Nov. 13.

Delta is working to resolve challenges with the airline’s weight and balance automation system. These delays are not related to any FAA air traffic systems. Please check with Delta for the latest information. https://t.co/q4Fc59VMYg.

The outage was resolved Sunday afternoon.

As of Monday morning, Delta’s delay rate was down to 6%.

While resolved fairly quickly, the system failure could hardly have come at a worse time. Millions of Americans are flying this week ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, and there are concerns that technology outages could again snarl air traffic during the busiest time of the year. The single busiest day for air travel is expected to be Sunday, Nov. 29, after Thanksgiving.

Recent findings suggest that there’s… a lot… of coverage surrounding the revamped Chase Sapphire Reserve Card. As per usual these days, the hot takes are plentiful and people are fired up. It’s either the apocalypse or the beginning of something great, depending on which attention seeker you read. As a long time cardholder, I’m really intrigued by the newly introduced changes.

The changes really fit my profile and sure, the card will cost more, but I won’t have to introduce any behavior change to get more, unlike some other cards. I’ll do most of my spending on this card. I’m a keeper just from the fee credit and earning multipliers.

But what about the redemption of points?

Industry observers note that well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners. It’s already a huge win.

Chase Travel’s ‘The Edit’ is a curated selection of nice hotels, which offer benefits similar to those provided by a travel agent or other luxury credit card booking platform. When booking a ‘The Edit’ property, you can expect breakfast for two, a $100 F&B credit, late check out and an upgrade subject to availability.

Which leads me to the important bit! With the revamped Sapphire Reserve Card, there’s a upcoming “Points Boost” feature, which offers up to two cents per point (25,000 points would cover $500, etc) for some flight or hotel purchases.

This can be amazing value, with flights of $3,000 being grabbed for just 150,000 points, with no taxes and fees and the ability to still earn frequent flyer miles and elite status points, since the airline treats it like a cash ticket.

Previously, the Sapphire Reserve card offered a steady point redemption opportunity directly on Chase Travel at 1.5 cents per point (100,000 points would cover $1500, etc). But with the latest version, some travel purchases you want to redeem for will either offer less value than before, the same, or more, with this new ‘Points Boost’ at 2 cents per point. We like more!

Sources indicate that I am in Newly introduced York and wanted to do a little staycation, so I fired up Chase Travel and found one of my more reliable upper mid-scale hotels, The Thompson Central Park was on as part of ‘The Edit’. My two options became a very clear singular, third option.

Industry observers note that typically, I’d consider paying cash or transferring my points from Chase to Hyatt to pay for a stay like this. Hyatt has “fixed” points rates, meaning the points price is largely irrespective of the cash price and only changes by seasonal dates. For this season, it was 25,000 points per night for the Thompson Central Park.

Industry observers note that if I were to transfer my points, I’d get a free night (the cash rate was around $500) and have a really solid points redemption at exactly two cents per point. I’m not loyal to any hotel chain really, so I wouldn’t get any breakfast or “elite” benefits, but a free night is a free night.

It has been revealed that BUT — Chase Travel had a ‘Points Boost’ option to book the hotel directly on their platform and not transfer points to Hyatt. Chase Travel was offering this property for circa 25,000 points and that would cover the $500 cash rate, but unlike transferring points to Hyatt, because I was redeeming a ‘The Edit’ property on Chase Travel, I’d receive….

Sources indicate that yep, by NOT transferring my points (and dealing with the fractured transfer journey) I was able to get myself basically $200 in additional value added to my stay with the breakfast and $100 property credit, not factoring in the value of late check out or a category room upgrade. In addition, I’ll be able to earn elite nights and Hyatt Points on the stay.

It has been revealed that A mere 25,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards Points got me a “free” $500 hotel night, breakfast for two, and $100 to spend at the hotel. That’s a pretty stunning redemption, giving more than two cents per point of value and still allowing me to earn on the stay, unlike when you transfer your points to a loyalty program. I wish I could’ve stayed longer.

For the first time I can remember, transferring points to Hyatt was not the best option here and that’s something to stand up and take notice of.

In a recent development, if Chase can keep up this Points Boost game, it can really send ripples through rewards. For the first time, people can easily receive tremendous value for their points through a credit card portal while still earning elite status and points with the hotel or airline of their choosing.

Sources indicate that you can check out the new 100,000 point + 500 travel credit offer for the Sapphire Reserve. It’s 200,000 points for Sapphire Reserve Business Cards.

It has been revealed that powerful storms bringing high winds and the potential for flooding could seriously disrupt commercial air travel in the U.S. during the single busiest week of the year.

It has been revealed that forecasters are warning that storm systems will likely strike parts of the South, Mid-Atlantic, and Northeast, as well as Northern California and the Pacific Northwest. These regions are home to some of the nation’s busiest airports, through which millions of American travelers will pass this week en route to visit family and friends for Thanksgiving on Thursday.

Recent findings suggest that in the Northeast, the remnants of a weakened, disorganized system were still clearing out on Monday. A much stronger storm is expected to develop in the Gulf of Mexico between Monday and Tuesday, impact parts of the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic Wednesday, and slam into the Fresh York metro area and New England on Thanksgiving Day.

According to recent reports, according to an advisory from the National Weather Service’s Weather Prediction Center, strong wind gusts up to 50 mph will be felt from the Carolinas to Maine. Flooding and beach erosion could be seen in coastal areas due to the already high tides.

WPC has initiated Key Messages for a Thanksgiving Coastal Storm that is expected to impact the U.S. East Coast. pic.twitter.com/pdQuU4U4yG.

Americans traveling from, through, or to these areas should prepare for the possibility of flooded roads, damage from high winds, and power outages, the agency stated.

NYC Emergency Management said Sunday that the storm could bring gusts of 40 to 45 mph and about one to two inches of rain to the city.

Recent findings suggest that for Fresh York and New England, the storm will be at its strongest Thursday evening. Parts of the Adirondacks and northern New England could see ice and snow mixed in with rain.

In California, Oregon, and Washington, residents still recovering from flooding last week could be hit again by rain and strong winds. A newly introduced system is expected to move in Tuesday and Wednesday; combined with the “king tides,” the storm could cause flooding up and down the West Coast.

Sources indicate that the impact is expected to be most severe between Portland, Oregon, and San Francisco. San Francisco’s mayor said residents should take the forecasts seriously and consider not traveling for the holiday.

The Sierra Nevada, meanwhile, will see fresh snow, meteorologists stated.

Industry observers note that over six million people are expected to fly within the U.S. this week for Thanksgiving. The surge is already underway, with many carriers adding flights to accommodate the increased traffic. American Airlines earlier this month projected its busiest Thanksgiving week since before the COVID-19 pandemic; that prediction could hold true for other U.S. airlines as well.

AirlineGeeks will continue to monitor weather conditions and provide updates as the week progresses.

FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.
  • Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.

Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.

The fate of the nominations and bills could ultimately be decided via a challenge on the Senate floor, according to a Democratic committee staffer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

In a statement Wednesday morning, committee Democrats, led by ranking member  Maria Cantwell of Washington, said they objected to Thumann Severs’ nomination without a Democratic “pair” nomination and referenced a letter they sent to Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Monday requesting the nomination be removed from the agenda.

Sources indicate that “Commissioner Anna Gomez could be re-nominated with all swiftness, as we have called for numerous times,” the group wrote. “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.”.

Thumann Severs, if confirmed, would give the FCC three Republican members and one Democrat, Gomez. The three Republicans could then constitute a quorum on the commission, allowing President Donald Trump to potentially fire Gomez. The commission generally has five members, three of the president’s party and two in the minority.

Cruz noted at the markup that there is nothing in the law that requires moving nominees in pairs, and that committee Republicans would continue their work on what he called a nomination that followed a “typical process.”.

It has been revealed that “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January,” Cruz said. “But today is November 18th. The American people elected each of us to fulfill our duties, including advice and consent, for our full terms.”.

Related: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing.

The Democratic staffer told reporters that because the committee did not adopt rules at the beginning of the 119th Congress, it has been operating under rules from the 118th, which required the attendance of at least one member of the minority party to constitute a quorum for reporting bills or nominations.

“The remaining recourse is to basically go to the floor and . . . make an inquiry in terms of what took place today, and then there would have to be a formal ruling by the chair,” they said.

They added that in determining whether the committee had a quorum to advance the nomination, “It would depend on how they view our committee rules from the 118th that we practice under for the 119th versus what the Senate rules are.” The staffer said they have not yet spoken with committee Democrats or Democratic leadership about looks for such an inquiry.

Industry observers note that democrats also previously boycotted a committee markup in March over an aviation safety bill left off the committee’s agenda, after which action was deferred. The committee later came to agreement and rescheduled the markup.

In their letter Monday, Democrats quoted Cruz from a 2014 statement about the nomination of Loretta Lynch to be attorney general.

“As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the letter remarked.

On Tuesday, Sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., wrote his own letter to Cruz calling for the removal of the nomination from the agenda based on grounds that Thumann Severs lied to the committee.

Sources indicate that “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related issues,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount,” Luján wrote.

Democrats have criticized the FCC and Carr for allowing media consolidation, including by Skydance. There has also been bipartisan criticism of Carr’s threats against broadcasters for speech he disagrees with.

Luján told reporters Wednesday prior to the markup that he expects, under Democratic control next year, Carr and potentially Thumann Severs would be called to testify.

“I have questions. I certainly hope that Brendan Carr will voluntarily show up to this committee when invited, and that other rules and tools do not need to be used,” Luján mentioned, responding to a question about possibly subpoenaing Carr. “But . . . everything should be on the table.”.

Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., remarked at the markup that he spoke with Thumann Severs about her role at the FCC and her “lack of engagement” as the commission has made decisions regarding broadcasters. He also said he found her testimony at last week’s nomination hearing “comforting.”.

According to recent reports, “I have concerns with FCC action in regard to political speech, broadcasters, and she indicated in her answers . . . in a way that provided me with a level of comfort about her nomination in regard to that issue,” Moran said.

Moran also stated he hopes to meet with Thumann Severs before her nomination is brought to the floor.

  • Recent findings suggest that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen.
  • Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Recent findings suggest that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders said Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care proposal if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

It has been revealed that sanders noted Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

According to recent reports, his version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

It has been revealed that “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders remarked, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion proposal, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of Newly introduced York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders said he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

Industry observers note that in addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

Industry observers note that sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., remarked last week that he prepares to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee challenges, he looks forward to finding common ground.

Breaking: American Airlines Expands Block On Last-Minute Partner Award Bookings

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, american Airlines appears to have expanded a frustrating restriction on last-minute award travel.
  • As first flagged by One Mile At A Time, American is now withholding saver award inventory on wholly domestic connecting itineraries within 144 hours of departure.
  • American began blocking domestic nonstop saver awards within that window in May.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, american Airlines appears to have expanded a frustrating restriction on last-minute award travel. Domestic connections are now subject to the same six-day cutoff that already blocked nonstop saver awards through partner programs. For travelers using Alaska Atmos Rewards points or British Airways Avios, another useful way to book American flights seems to have vanished.

As first flagged by One Mile At A Time, American is now withholding saver award inventory on wholly domestic connecting itineraries within 144 hours of departure. The restriction affects both economy and premium cabins.

American began blocking domestic nonstop saver awards within that window in May. Connections initially remained available, but that appears to have changed. International itineraries, including those with domestic connections, reportedly remain outside this restriction.

When using AA miles, there appears to be no change. AAdvantage members can still book flights through American itself, where award prices vary. The restriction concerns the inventory that other frequent flyer programs need to sell an award on American.

First, a short primer…each day this blog has folks who have read it for almost 20 years and those who are reading it for the first time.

A seat available for miles on AA.com is not necessarily available to Alaska or British Airways. American controls what it releases to those programs, and its own award pricing varies by flight and date.

When the original restriction emerged, flights disappeared from partner searches as they crossed the six-day threshold, even while remaining available through AAdvantage.

So an empty search result on a partner website does not necessarily mean the flight is full or that American has stopped accepting miles. It may simply mean you have the wrong kind of miles….

I understand why American might prefer that someone book through AAdvantage rather than redeem another airline’s currency. Giving travelers a reason to accumulate its own miles has commercial value and is part of AA’s strategy to return to profitability.

But understanding the incentive does not make this a welcome development.

It has been revealed that one of the most useful things about miles is being able to arrange a trip when cash fares are high. Think family emergency or holiday travel.

According to recent reports, in those circumstances, having access to American through another program can be very valuable. Removing that option makes the points already sitting in those accounts less useful, even if the published award chart does not change.

We spend plenty of time discussing award price increases, but availability deserves just as much attention. An attractive mileage price is of little practical value when the program cannot book the flight you need, which is frequent criticism of Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards, now even less valuable than due to AA blocking space.

No one is asking American to release every unsold seat to every partner….AA has every right to monetize as many seats as it can, just like it doing with first class upgrades.

Still, I would rather see American manage availability flight by flight than impose a broad cutoff based on how soon someone wants to travel. A flight with weak demand and a flight that is nearly sold out do not present the same commercial circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that american does not comment on program changes like this, but has apparently concluded that the additional control is worth the lost partner bookings. Without knowing the reimbursement arrangements, I am not going to pretend I can calculate that trade-off.

According to recent reports, from the passenger perspective, however, this is another reason to temper expectations about airline partnerships. The ability to earn points in one program and redeem them across a network is a major selling point. Restrictions like this make that promise less useful…and this is hardly a unique trend: we see the same thing with Delta and United.

If you need an American flight within six days of departure, check AAdvantage directly, for now that is your only option. Always compare the mileage price with the cash fare too…using miles is not automatically the better deal and is often not.

For travel farther out, I would still compare partner options before booking. But I would be certainly not transfer points speculatively while hoping that domestic American availability will open shortly before departure.

The expansion of partner award blocking removes another option for travelers hoping to use miles for last-minute domestic American flights. AAdvantage remains an option, but it’s a big blow to Alaska Airlines Atmos members.

Sources indicate that I understand why American wants to favor its own program. Even so, I cannot celebrate this news.

    It has been revealed that trends come and go, but here at Condé Nast Traveler, one thing never changes: your insatiable appetite for seeing the world. This year, our readers cast an almighty 798,867 votes in our 39th Readers’ Choice Awards to tell us about the planet’s best travel experiences: You fell hard for palace hotels in Morocco, cruised down the Amazon, and got swept up in New York City’s exhilarating energy. Now, read on to find out where your favorites fall among the winners—and get inspired for where to go next, whether it's to a top-rated hotel or resort, or centered around a worthy cruise, spa, or island. These are the best resorts in the world as voted by you, our readers.

    View this gallery as a list of the top resorts in the Caribbean with scores here.

    Anse Chastanet is a retreat for active travelers who enjoy its unique open-air luxury, whether enjoying a romantic honeymoon, scuba diving in the Soufriere Marine Management Area, or just exploring eco-paradise. The 600-acre, 51-accommodation property has two soft sand beaches, four restaurants, three bars, and enough options—from jungle biking on the property’s trails, to snorkeling with a marine biologist, to playing pickleball, to a chocolate-focused treatment menu at Kai Belté Spa —to keep guests as active or relaxed as they prefer. The resort can also arrange unforgettable romantic experiences like an ultra-luxe private sunset catamaran sailing or a Private Castaway Beach Dinner. Many of the rooms feature either open-air louvered walls or true open-air walls, with each room individually designed and carefully angled with privacy in mind. Many rooms feature stunning views of the Caribbean, the Pitons, or both. The gorgeous property is located on a steep hillside with many stairs, uneven pathways, and no elevators, so access may be a challenge for people with limited mobility.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    In a recent development, the namesake hillside resort set above Toiny Bay gives “wild” an unexpected latest meaning when it comes to sceney St. Barts. On the shrubby southeastern point of the island, this unfussy haven is where an in-the-know social set head to find serenity. The star amenity here is the private beach, accessible via a three-minute Defender ride down switchbacking roads. Le Toiny’s stretch of soft sand is considered the sole private hotel beach on all of St. Barts. Plus, some of the oldest traditional English-style cottages on the island, dating back to the 1700s, can be found beside the beach club (one is right now used as treatment areas for the spa). The suites and villas were redesigned in 2024 to create airy living spaces that draw your eye outward to the leafy open-air surroundings and azure water views just beyond your private pool deck.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Recent findings suggest that grand Cayman may be famous for its SCUBA diving and offshore banking, but with several daily non-stops from New York and Boston, it’s increasingly drawing families to its powdery, placid western Caribbean beaches. On the island’s Seven Mile Beach—one of the loveliest stretches of sand in the world—you'll find the 266-room Kimpton Seafire Resort & Spa, with a boutique atmosphere that manages to be both child-friendly (two pools, a kids club) and hip (colorful, contemporary design, and a lobby scene replete with pool table, library, and daily happy hour). The food is also strong: Hit beachside Coccoloba for fish tacos and ceviches; Ave, the resort's primary restaurant, for epic breakfast buffets (including house-made cronuts); and the sceney Avecita for progressive Spanish fare like white anchovy toast and prawn tartare, served up alongside craft cocktails at the chef’s counter. You can always snorkel and parasail right off the hotel’s beach, but you’re also just a short ride from Stingray City (where you can stand on a sandbar and touch giant rays as they swim by), world-class gardens (look for the endangered blue iguana), golf, and roadside jerk chicken. Hit Rum Point to toast the sunset—or maybe you'll prefer doing that from your own private balcony.

    Industry observers note that this romantic all-suite beachfront retreat north of the sprawling all-inclusives of Punta Cana is a diamond literally in the rough—the last two miles of the approach road are so bone rattling that it may be worth ponying up more than $250 for the ten-minute helicopter transfer from the airport in Punta Cana. But behind the resort’s unmarked security gate, Zoëtry is breathtaking. The open-air lobby has a soaring peaked thatch roof, and the 51rooms, divided between two-story thatched buildings and freestanding villas, are arranged around two snaking pools and are no more than a one-minute walk from the beach. With classic clean lines, they are dramatic by virtue of their size (the smallest is 775 square feet) and simple comforts—wicker ceilings, dark hardwood floors and furniture, white-on-white beds, immense bathrooms with black slate showers and deep soaking tubs. The resort’s restaurants draw culinary inspiration from traditional Dominican fare and international flavors, with an emphasis on using locally grown and organic ingredients.

    In a recent development, for toes-in-the-sand luxury with impeccable service, foodie-approved eateries, Caribbean-cool rooms, and views that will have all your friends and family seeing green, La Samanna can’t be beat. Set along the white sands of Baie Longue, known for being one of the most beautiful beaches in all of St. Martin, guests are never far from the startlingly turquoise waters, and La Samanna offers plenty of ways to get out on the water, including complimentary kayaks, paddleboards, snorkeling gear, and more. With three main restaurants—one of which changes in concept between lunch and dinner—plus a fabulous daily breakfast and top-notch room service, there’s really no reason to leave for meals. The star of the show is L’Oursin, the upscale French restaurant just off the lobby, where each table comes with a view of the sailboat-spotted sea. If you can, splurge on one of the property's eight independent villas—the double-level mansions have everything a group could need to vacation more than comfortably.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Industry observers note that the "secret" part of Secret Bay's name is no accident—the resort's 10 gorgeous villas give new meaning to the word hideaway. Touches vary from villa to villa, but all have interiors and floors made of Guyanese Greenheart, bedroom furniture made of Dominican red cedar, open decks, private pools, and 180-degree views over the mountain peaks of Dominica and the Caribbean Sea. Though we doubt you'll get tired of living your own castaway fantasies (albeit with much nicer accommodations), Secret Bay's concierge is available to help craft personalized itineraries: think rainforest hikes with a famed naturalist, or a sunset sail along the island's western coast.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Anguilla is a small-but-mighty island packed with a handful of luxury properties, dining options, and a whole bunch of outstanding beaches. Barnes Bay and Meads Bay surround the property on both sides, with waters that are occasionally rough but known to be swimmable at other times of the year. Regardless of the conditions, white beach chairs line the sand in pristine formation each morning, and three large pool areas—two kid-friendly, and one adults-only—provide plenty of swimming options when the ocean is unavailable. The property stretches across the shore, which means each room provides a unique view of some combination of the wide property’s beachfront, ocean, palm trees, or garden areas. In the ocean-view one-bedroom suite, we overlooked the modernist pool deck as well as the distant ocean, with a plunge pool on the balcony and ample outdoor space for afternoon lounging. The bathroom was equipped with two sinks, a large tub, and a marble walk-in shower.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    All rooms at this Sandals Resort are in stone buildings on a two-mile-long beach in a 500-acre wilderness preserve on the island's south coast. The resort is arranged as three European villages—Dutch, French, and Italian (including a Venetian piazza)—and the architecture includes lots of marble columns and vaulted ceilings. "Buildings are spread out, but it still feels like an intimate retreat." Rooms differ according to village: French rooms have mahogany four-poster beds and Caribbean decor, while Italian rooms are heavy on marble. The plantation-style Eleanor's, complete with a waterwheel and a stone fireplace, serves contemporary Caribbean cuisine.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Though the Buccaneer, on the U.S. Virgin Island of St. Croix, has been proudly run by the Armstrong family for over 70 years—it's the longest-running resort in the Caribbean—its history dates even further back to the property's earliest construction by a Knight of Malta in 1653. Since then, it's been a private home; a sugar mill; a cotton estate, then a cattle estate; and now, an incredibly warm, family-friendly resort that's more like a country club. You have access to an 18-hole golf course, eight tennis courts, three beaches (whether you prefer kayaking and snorkeling or lounging in peace and quiet), a full water sports center, and none of the pretense. Arrive for lunch at the Grotto in your bathing suit, and please don't sleep through the terrific breakfast buffet. The Buccanneer knows how to put out a spread. Once you're done moving about for the day, settle into the deluxe oceanfront room—the resort's most popular—and lie on your bed beneath the 16-foot-high wood ceilings, watching the waves lap the beach out your picture window.

    The tiny volcanic island of Grenada is both an unexpected and obvious choice for Six Senses’ foray into the Caribbean. Compared to significant-hitting neighbors like St. Lucia and Antigua, it has been overlooked by travelers to the region. But this means that it remains largely uncrowded and retains a more rustic version of tourism. Six Senses has done well to anchor itself to that. Here, your welcome ritual begins with a sensory spice “tour;” its 56 suites and 15 villas are stylish but designed to sit unobtrusively on the landscape; and its curated excursions—from rainforest hikes to Rastafarian farm visits—spotlight the best of Grenada’s natural bounty. In classic Six Senses style, wellness is a key protagonist, and you can seek out everything from aerial yoga to sleep therapy, as well as treatments like the Caribbean Cleansing Ritual that nod to the surroundings. It’s very tempting to stay put, heading to the spa or sipping rum cocktails poolside, but you’d do well to pair off with one of the property’s community hosts and head out: to spice-laden markets in its photogenic capital or for a bit of beachside limin’ (defined locally as “kicking with friends”), a beloved national pastime.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    The old adage of getting what you pay for rings true here, and while it may be a splurge, it will be an unforgettable stay. The rooms are quiet, the beds are comfortable, and in my opinion, this is the best stretch of beach on the island. If you’re looking for luxury—and budget isn’t an issue—the Ritz is the top of the line. Guests who stay in the 320 spacious and chic rooms can expect to be spoiled. Servers cruise around the shore on Segway scooters, effortlessly balancing trays of tropical cocktails. The concierge can secure reservations for you at sold-out restaurants, set up offsite tours, and suggest itineraries for any kind of traveler. The 15,000-square-foot spa at the Ritz is one of the largest and best on the island, and the property's on-site restaurants are simply divine. The vibe is upscale without being stuffy, with guests in the elevators side by side wearing pool towels and Prada.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    A relatively newly introduced addition to St. Barts' luxury hotel scene, Le Barthélemy is a sophisticated winner that keeps with the island's low-rise sensibility. Set between a lagoon and Grand Cul-de-Sac beach along the island's northeastern shore, the hotel is an education in understated elegance. Rooms are spare and enormous, with lots of wood and one or two pops of bright color—some even have small, rectangular plunge pools for mini-laps. The food at  Amis St. Barth is unabashedly modern French, with attention paid to proper portions in the tropics: in other words, not too much. Water sports enthusiasts have an expanse of calm shallow waters for kayaking, kite-surfing, and snorkeling—a flotilla of a dozen sea turtles that survived the storms of 2017 remain in residence and are easily visible.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    It has been revealed that those who knew and loved Le Carl Gustaf the first time around will have even more reason to fall for it now that the Barriere group has taken over. The hotelier company—known for reviving particularly beloved but withering properties—has made sure to keep the spirit of Le Carl chic and easy. The raw wood and petite terraces still make it feel like the beach house of a fabulous French friend, yet the hotel’s reimagined approach to the environment gives it a 21st-century edge. Paris design firm Gilles and Boissier gussied up the 21 rooms with creams, stone, and linen, as well as a profusion of palms separating various spaces with a curtain of greenery. Suites have been reconfigured to catch sea breezes, providing natural air conditioning. And a fleet of electric bikes brings guests down the hill upon which the hotel stands like a lookout, over the town and coastline, to nearby Shell Beach, the perfect place for a picnic prepared by the hotel’s staff that feels, appropriately simple and chic—much like Le Carl itself.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Romance is taken to a whole other level at this adults-only St. Lucia resort. With 36 plunge pool suites, butler service, and a personalized bar with only the top-shelf, this enclave was made for couples to relax and reconnect. While there's no shortage of places to lounge or splash around in on property, the resort also offers an array of excursions to explore the gorgeous corner of the Caribbean St. Lucia lays claim to. From rainforest nature walks with a fully packed picnic basket to adrenaline-pumping ATV tours, Serenity at Coconut Bay knows there's many ways to take in all the gorgeous scenery.

    #214571. Restored to Calder’s strategy, the clouds are spinning again

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1161 w)
